解珍，登州人氏，与兄弟解宝同为登州城外猎户出身，世居山乡，以打猎为生。解氏兄弟自.en:
Xie Zhen came from Dengzhou. He and his younger brother Xie Bao belonged to a family of hunters who had long lived in the hills outside the city. Trained from childhood, they wielded steel hunting forks, captured tigers in the mountains and hunted wild beasts in the woods with exceptional courage. Many dangerous animals of the Dengzhou hills fell to them. Xie Zhen was tall and imposing, with a fiery temper and ruthless decisiveness. He was called the Two-Headed Snake; Xie Bao was the Double-Tailed Scorpion. Both names invoked venomous creatures, warning that these fierce brothers were dangerous to provoke.

The brothers wore animal skins, carried sharp blades at their waists and hunted through Dengzhou's forests with solid-iron, steel-tipped forks. They also set spring bows and poisoned arrows to take tigers and leopards. When a white-browed tiger began killing people, the prefect ordered the hunters to destroy it by a fixed deadline. Acting on the official order, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao set their traps and wounded the beast. It rolled down a cliff into the rear garden of Old Master Mao's estate. The brothers went to claim its body, but Mao wanted the official reward for himself. He denied seeing the tiger and accused them of robbery and violence in broad daylight.

Mao's son Mao Zhongyi conspired with the local military superintendent and bribed Dengzhou's officials. The brothers were arrested, tortured into confessions and placed on death row. Their innocent lives seemed lost until their cousin Gu Dasao, the Tigress, learned of their plight. A bold, generous tavern keeper devoted to her kin, she planned a prison rescue with her husband Sun Xin. He summoned his elder brother Sun Li, Dengzhou's military constable known as Sickly Yuchi, together with Zou Yuan, his nephew Zou Run, Yue He and other heroes. Working from within and without, they broke into the jail, freed the Xie brothers and killed the Mao household in revenge.

With no safe home after the jailbreak, the group set out for Liangshan. Its army was then engaged in the third assault on Zhu Manor. Sun Li had studied alongside the manor's instructor Luan Tingyu, so he devised a false submission: the newcomers would pretend to help the manor while serving as inside agents. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao entered with Sun Li and Gu Dasao. When Liangshan attacked, they turned on the defenders and joined the assault from inside. The brothers fought bravely at the front and earned their place among Liangshan's leaders.

At the great assembly, Xie Zhen ranked thirty-fourth among the Heavenly Spirits, corresponding to the Heavenly Violent Star. He and Xie Bao commanded infantry. Their hunting background made them skilled at mountain travel, climbing, concealment and ambush, so Liangshan often sent them ahead when high ground or dangerous forest routes had to be crossed. They also served in the attacks on Zengtou, Dongping and Dongchang.

After the imperial amnesty, Xie Zhen fought against Liao, Tian Hu and Wang Qing across north and south. During the campaign against Fang La, the army approached the steep Wulong Ridge, whose pass stood high on the summit. The brothers volunteered to scale the cliffs at night and surprise its garrison. They climbed by vines and roots, but the defenders discovered them and sent logs and rocks crashing down, then caught them with hooks. Exhausted on the cliff face, Xie Zhen lost his grip and fell with his weapons into a rocky ravine. Xie Bao was likewise killed below by arrows, spears and halberds. Both died that day at Wulong Ridge. Xie Zhen's life began in the injustice of a tiger hunt in Dengzhou and ended on a perilous southern cliff. Hunter and fork-bearer to the last, he shared his brother's life and death: two loyal, courageous men who never abandoned each other, and whose fate invites lasting sorrow.
解珍，登州人氏，与兄弟解宝同为登州城外猎户出身，世居山乡，以打猎为生。解氏兄弟自.ja:
解珍は登州の人で、弟の解宝とともに城外の山里に代々暮らす猟師の家に生まれた。幼い頃から技を磨き、鋼叉を得意とし、山で虎を捕らえ、林で獣を追う勇気は並外れていた。登州の山の猛獣は、多くが二人の手に倒れた。解珍は堂々とした体格と容貌を備え、気性は火のように激しく、行動は苛烈で決断が早い。「両頭蛇」と呼ばれ、弟の解宝は「双尾蠍」と呼ばれた。ともに毒を持つ生き物の名で、二頭の蛇、二尾の蠍のように、触れれば傷つく恐ろしい兄弟だという意味が込められている。

猟師の家に育った二人は獣皮をまとい、腰に刃を帯び、総鉄の鋼先の叉を携えて登州の山林を歩いた。仕掛け弓や毒矢にも長け、虎豹を狩って暮らしていた。ある日、山に白い額の虎が出て人を害し、知府は期限を切って猟師に討伐を命じた。解珍と解宝は公文を受け、山に仕掛けを置いて虎を射た。虎は崖を転がり、麓の毛太公の屋敷の裏庭へ落ちた。二人が死骸を求めると、毛太公は褒賞を横取りしようと、虎など見ていないと偽り、逆に二人を白昼の強盗と暴行で訴えた。

毛太公の子・毛仲義は地元の兵馬都監と結託し、登州の官吏にも賄賂を送った。兄弟は捕らえられ、拷問で自白を強いられて死囚牢へ入れられ、命を奪われようとしていた。冤罪に苦しむ二人を救ったのは、従姉の顧大嫂である。「母大虫」と呼ばれる豪快な酒店の女主人は、親族を何より大切にしていた。事情を聞くと夫の孫新と牢破りを相談した。孫新は兄で登州兵馬提轄の「病尉遅」孫立、鄒淵と甥の鄒潤、楽和らを招いた。一同は内外から協力して登州の牢を破り、解珍と解宝を救い、毛太公一家を殺して恨みを晴らした。

牢破りの後は身を置く場所がなく、皆で梁山を目指した。折しも梁山は三たび祝家荘を攻めていた。孫立は荘の師範・欒廷玉と同門だったため、助勢を装って入り、内応する策を立てた。解珍と解宝も孫立、顧大嫂らと荘へ紛れ込み、梁山の攻撃に合わせて内側から兵を返した。内外の挟撃で祝家荘は破られ、先頭で勇敢に戦った兄弟は功を立て、仲間とともに梁山の頭領となった。

大聚義で解珍は天暴星に応じる天罡の第三十四位となり、解宝とともに歩軍頭領を務めた。猟師として山道、岩登り、隠密、伏撃に長けていたため、険しい山林や高所を越える際にはしばしば先発を任された。曾頭市、東平、東昌への攻撃にも力を尽くした。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶との戦いに加わり、南北を転戦した。方臘征討で軍が烏竜嶺へ迫ると、高い山頂に関所を構える険阻な地形が立ちはだかった。絶壁登りを得意とする兄弟は、夜に登って奇襲すると志願した。蔓や草の根をつかんで登ったが、守兵に見つかり、丸太と岩を落とされ、鉤でも掛けられた。解珍は崖で力尽きて手を滑らせ、武器もろとも深い谷の岩間へ落ちて死んだ。解宝も嶺の下で矢や槍戟を受け、同じ日に命を落とした。「両頭蛇」解珍は狩りを生業とし、叉を武器とし、登州の虎事件の冤罪から身を起こし、江南の絶壁で果てた。弟と生死をともにし、始めから終わりまで離れなかった忠勇の兄弟の運命は、聞く者を悲しませる。

徐宁者，东京人氏，原是金枪班的教师，于宫禁之中教演武艺，乃八十万禁军中一员有名的.en:
Xu Ning came from the capital and served as instructor of the Golden Spear Company, teaching martial skills within the palace precincts. Among the imperial guards he was a celebrated expert. His hooked lance was extraordinary, and his ancestral hooked-lance method was especially effective against cavalry. This skill earned him the name Golden Lancer. He knew Lin Chong, the Panther Head, from their service in the capital and was an old friend. A law-abiding man with no wish to become an outlaw, Xu Ning joined Liangshan only because he was tricked—a story of unusually elaborate ingenuity.

Liangshan was then facing the imperial general Huyan Zhuo, the Double Clubs. His chained-cavalry formation linked horses with iron rings in groups of thirty, armoring riders and mounts alike. Their charge struck like a collapsing mountain, repeatedly defeating Liangshan and inflicting heavy losses. Wu Yong searched for a counter and learned that only the hooked lance could break it. Xu Ning was the one master capable of teaching that method in battle. Wu Yong therefore devised a plan to lure him up the mountain.

Xu Ning treasured an ancestral suit of goose-feather-patterned Saitangni armor as dearly as his life. He kept it in a leather case suspended from his bedroom beam. Wu Yong sent Shi Qian, the Flea on a Drum, to the capital. Agile enough to cross roofs and walls, Shi Qian stole into the house at night and took the armor. Xu Ning discovered the theft the next day and searched frantically. Liangshan sent Yang Xiong, the Sickly Guan Suo, and Dai Zong, the Marvelous Traveler, to assist the plot. They deliberately left clues that drew Xu Ning farther and farther from the capital in pursuit of his heirloom. On the road, they drugged his food and wine, rendered him unconscious and carried him to Liangshan.

Waking there, Xu Ning realized the deception and was deeply distressed. He repeatedly refused to abandon his lawful life. Tang Long, his cousin and a central figure in the scheme, urged him to reconsider; Song Jiang and Wu Yong returned the armor and appealed to fellowship. With his treasure already on the mountain, his way back to the capital cut off, and the outlaws showing him earnest respect, he finally agreed. He drilled the troops day and night, passing on the whole ancestral art. In battle, Liangshan's hooked lances caught the horses' legs and brought Huyan Zhuo's formation crashing down. This decisive victory secured Xu Ning's place among the leaders.

At the great assembly, his teaching and destruction of the chained cavalry earned him eighteenth place among the Heavenly Spirits, corresponding to the Heavenly Assistance Star. He commanded cavalry and became an indispensable warrior-instructor. His refined hooked-lance technique won repeated distinctions in later campaigns, marking him as one of Liangshan's finest mounted fighters.

After amnesty, Xu Ning served Song Jiang against Liao and Fang La. In fierce fighting during the attack on Hangzhou, he pursued an enemy officer and was struck by an arrow fired from concealment. Its head was poisoned. Despite treatment, the poison could not be cured. When the army later reached Xiuzhou, he died of the wound. A gifted general whose ancestral skill had broken a formidable formation was lost to a single poisoned arrow. Rather than a clear death at the battlefront, he succumbed slowly to its venom. His hooked-lance art and treasured Saitangni armor passed into memory, leaving the name Golden Lancer to later generations.
徐宁者，东京人氏，原是金枪班的教师，于宫禁之中教演武艺，乃八十万禁军中一员有名的.ja:
徐寧は東京の出身で、金槍班の師範として宮中で武芸を教え、八十万禁軍の名手の一人とされた。鈎鎌槍を自在に操り、とりわけ騎兵を破る家伝の鈎鎌槍法で知られ、「金槍手」と呼ばれた。豹子頭の林冲とは京師の禁軍で勤めた旧知の仲である。もとは法を守って暮らし、山賊になる気などなかった。その梁山入りはすべて「欺いて誘う」ことから始まり、水滸の中でも巧妙な一話となった。

当時、梁山泊は官軍の大将「双鞭」呼延灼と対峙していた。呼延灼の連環馬は三十頭を一組に鉄環でつなぎ、人も馬も甲を着け、山が崩れるように突進する。梁山軍は何度も敗れ、損失を重ねて打つ手がなかった。呉用が破陣の方法を探すと、鈎鎌槍だけが対抗でき、その槍法を熟知して実地に教えられるのは徐寧ただ一人だと分かった。そこで徐寧を山へ誘い込む策が立てられた。

徐寧の家には、雁の羽根を敷き詰めたような家宝の賽唐猊の甲があった。命ほどに大切にし、革の箱へ入れて寝室の梁から吊っていた。呉用は「鼓上蚤」時遷を東京へ送った。屋根や壁を自在に越える時遷は夜に家へ忍び込み、宝甲を盗み去った。翌朝に盗難を知った徐寧は、焦って各所を探し回った。梁山は「病関索」楊雄や「神行太保」戴宗らにも援護させ、わざと宝甲の手がかりを残した。徐寧は家宝を取り戻そうと、知らず知らず東京を離れ、遠くまで追い続けた。道中では酒食に蒙汗薬を入れられ、眠らされたまま梁山へ運ばれた。

梁山で目覚めた徐寧は騙されたと知り、大いに悔やんだ。良民である自分は山賊になりたくないと何度も断ったが、従兄弟で策の要でもあった湯隆が説得した。宋江と呉用も甲を返し、義を尽くして繰り返し話した。家宝は山にあり、京へ戻る道も失い、皆の誠意にも感じて、徐寧はついに入伙を承諾した。以後は昼夜軍士を鍛え、家伝の槍法を余さず教えた。戦の日、梁山兵は鈎鎌槍で馬脚を掛け、呼延灼の連環馬を人馬もろとも倒して官軍を大破した。この大功で徐寧の梁山での地位は確かなものとなった。

大聚義では、槍法の伝授と連環馬を破った功により天罡に列し、天祐星に応じる第十八位となった。馬軍を率い、教頭でも猛将でもある欠かせぬ存在となる。精妙な鈎鎌槍法で後の戦いでも幾度も功を立て、馬軍の名手として働いた。

招安後は宋江に従って遼と方臘を討った。杭州攻略の激戦で敵将を追っていた時、敵兵が陰から放った矢に当たった。矢先には毒が塗られていた。治療を受けても毒は解けず、後に軍が秀州へ着いた頃、重い傷で陣中に没した。家伝の絶技で難敵の陣を破った優れた将が、一本の毒矢で失われた。堂々たる戦場での最期ではなく、毒に蝕まれて死んだことは惜しまれる。その槍法と賽唐猊の宝甲は語り草となり、「金槍手」の名が後世へ残された。

丑郡马宣赞，乃梁山泊七十二地煞之一，应地杰星，坐第四十把交椅，为马军小彪将。此人.en:
Xuan Zan, the Ugly Prince Consort, was one of Liangshan's seventy-two Earthly Fiends. Corresponding to the Earthly Outstanding Star, he occupied the fortieth seat and served as a junior cavalry commander. His face was dark as the bottom of a pot, his nostrils turned upward, and he had curly hair and a red beard. Before joining Liangshan he was an imperial military officer, serving among the eight mounted guards before Xuanhe Hall and holding defensive and loyalty-service titles. Though strikingly unattractive, he was skilled with a steel saber, drew a powerful bow and shot accurately, on horseback or on foot.

His nickname arose from an unfortunate marriage. On the frontier, Xuan Zan once impressed a young northern enemy officer with a rapid succession of arrows. A prince admired his skill so much that he chose him to marry his daughter, making him a princely consort. The young princess was of noble birth and great beauty. After the wedding, she saw her husband's appearance and became miserable with aversion and resentment. Before long she fell ill from grief and died. Xuan Zan lost his wife, and his looks also hindered his official career. The name Ugly Prince Consort preserved the awkward tale of the ugly husband whose beautiful princess died in distress.

For all his appearance, Xuan Zan recognized talent. After Huyan Zhuo's defeat at Liangshan shook the court, Grand Preceptor Cai Jing gathered officials to discuss a response. Xuan Zan recommended Guan Sheng, inspector of Pudong, a direct descendant of Guan Yu and known as the Great Blade. He knew Guan Sheng's unmatched courage and mastery of military books and strongly urged that he take command. Cai Jing approved, summoned Guan Sheng and appointed him commanding officer, with Xuan Zan and Hao Siwen, the Wood Dog of the Well, as his deputies. Their fifteen thousand troops marched toward Liangshan under a diversionary plan: threaten its home base to relieve Lingzhou.

Guan Sheng fought repeated engagements below Liangshan, with Xuan Zan and Hao Siwen guarding his flanks and showing their own prowess. But Liangshan had many able commanders and Wu Yong's calculations. Guan Sheng fell into a false-surrender trap coordinated from within and without, and all three were captured. Respecting Guan Sheng's loyal ancestry and heroic skill, Song Jiang came down personally, untied him, bowed and treated him with honor. Moved by this fellowship, Guan Sheng joined Liangshan with both deputies. Xuan Zan thereafter served as a cavalry leader under his command.

When the heroes took their seats at the great assembly, Xuan Zan ranked fortieth among the Earthly Fiends. He and Hao Siwen remained Guan Sheng's right and left deputies, charging into battle and supporting each other. He fought in the two victories over Tong Guan and three over Gao Qiu, contributing his steel saber and fine archery as a dependable subordinate.

After amnesty, Xuan Zan followed Song Jiang north against Liao and south against Fang La, earning repeated merit through hard campaigning. Yet the one hundred and eight suffered terrible losses on reaching the southern provinces. At Changzhou, he joined the assault and fought an enemy general without retreating, but was overwhelmed and killed in the turmoil beneath the city walls. His life had been troubled: burdened by an unkind nickname, widowed, and finally buried far from home. Still, his judgment in recommending the worthy and his courage in battle were honorable qualities that more than justified calling him a hero.
丑郡马宣赞，乃梁山泊七十二地煞之一，应地杰星，坐第四十把交椅，为马军小彪将。此人.ja:
「醜郡馬」宣賛は梁山泊の七十二地煞の一人で、地傑星に応じ、第四十位に座った馬軍の小彪将である。顔は鍋底のように黒く、鼻孔は上を向き、巻き毛に赤い髭という醜い容貌だった。もとは朝廷の武官で、宣和殿前の八驃騎を務め、衙門防禦使・保義使の職も帯びていた。だが武芸は確かで、鋼刀を使い、強弓を引いてよく射ち、馬上でも徒歩でも腕を発揮した。

「醜郡馬」の名には、笑うに笑えぬ縁があった。かつて辺境で北方の若い将と勝負し、続けざまに矢を放つ妙技で相手を心服させた。その腕をある郡王が見込み、美しい郡主の娘の婿に迎えたのである。ところが高貴な姫は結婚後に夫の醜さを見て、嫌悪と悲しみに沈み、ほどなく心を病んで亡くなった。妻を失った宣賛は、その顔のため仕官の道も思うように進まなかった。「醜郡馬」というあだ名は、醜い婿が美しい郡主を悲しませて死なせたという、気の毒な過去を伝えるものとなった。

容貌は醜くても、宣賛は英雄と才を見抜く人物だった。呼延灼の梁山討伐が敗れ、朝廷が揺れると、太師蔡京は対策を協議した。そこで宣賛は、蒲東の巡検で、漢寿亭侯関羽の直系の子孫とされる「大刀」関勝を推薦した。万人に敵する勇と兵書への通暁を知っていたため、指揮官にふさわしいと強く推したのである。蔡京は関勝を召して領兵指揮使とし、宣賛と「井木犴」郝思文を左右の副将に任じた。一万五千の軍は梁山へ向かい、本拠を脅かして凌州を救う「囲魏救趙」の策を取った。

梁山の麓へ来た関勝は好漢たちと戦いを重ね、宣賛と郝思文は左右の翼として武威を示した。だが梁山には多くの兵将と呉用の策があり、関勝は偽降と内外呼応の計にかかり、三人とも捕らえられた。宋江は関勝の忠義の血筋と武勇を重んじ、自ら堂を下りて縄を解き、拝礼して厚遇した。その義に感じた関勝は二人の副将とともに梁山へ帰順した。以後、宣賛は馬軍頭領として関勝の麾下で出陣した。

大聚義の席次では地煞の第四十位となり、郝思文とともに関勝の左右の副将を務めた。突撃では互いに支え合い、童貫を二度、高俅を三度退ける大戦にも従軍した。鋼刀と弓の腕をもって力を尽くし、関勝の頼れる部将となった。

招安後は宋江の軍に従い、北の遼、南の方臘と戦い、鞍馬の塵にまみれて功を重ねた。しかし百八人が江南へ下ると、江浙で甚大な損失を受けた。常州攻略で宣賛は敵将と激しく戦い、一歩も退かなかったが、ついには多勢に抗しきれず、城下の乱戦で命を落とした。醜い名を負い、妻を失い、異郷に骨を埋めた波乱の一生である。それでも賢才を推す眼識と、戦場で命を尽くす忠勇は堂々たるもので、好漢の名に恥じるものではなかった。

薛永者,河南洛阳人氏也。其祖上原是军官出身,后来家道中落,薛永流落江湖,以使枪棒.en:
Xue Yong came from Luoyang in Henan. His ancestors had been military officers, but the family's fortunes declined, leaving him to wander and earn his living by demonstrating spear and staff skills and selling medicinal plasters. He was yellow-faced and thin, with a withered, sickly appearance, yet his martial skill was excellent. That contrast earned him the name Sickly Tiger. “Tiger” warned that despite his unhealthy look, his abilities were fierce and not to be underestimated. Anyone who judged him by appearance would be surprised by the vigor with which he wielded his weapons.

He first appeared at Jieyang Town, in an incident involving Mu Chun, the Little Unrestrained, and Song Jiang, the Timely Rain. Passing through the town on his way through Jiangzhou, Song Jiang found Xue Yong performing. The newcomer knew neither the place nor its people. Though his display drew a crowd, nobody cheered or gave money. Song Jiang pitied such neglect of real skill and gave him five taels of silver. But Jieyang was controlled by the brothers Mu Hong and Mu Chun: visiting performers had to pay their respects to the Mu household before they could work or receive rewards. Neither Xue Yong nor the traveler Song Jiang knew this rule. Mu Chun sprang forward, challenged Song Jiang and quarreled with Xue Yong. The resulting feud brought the Mu brothers and their men in pursuit of Song Jiang, driving him to the Xunyang River, where he nearly died before Li Jun, Zhang Heng and others rescued him. A street performance thus helped set in motion the great events that followed in Jiangzhou.

Later, Song Jiang's rebellious poem brought disaster in Jiangzhou. Framed by Huang Wenbing, he and Dai Zong were taken to the execution ground. Heroes from Liangshan and the Jiangzhou region stormed the city and rescued both. After this gathering, Mu Hong and Mu Chun from Jieyang, Li Jun, Zhang Heng, Zhang Shun, Tong Wei and Tong Meng from the river, and the performer Xue Yong all followed Song Jiang to Liangshan. Xue Yong abandoned his street trade and became a stronghold leader.

He also earned merit after joining. When Liangshan attacked Daming to rescue Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu, Wu Yong ordered him to disguise himself as a beggar. He slipped inside, hid in a ruined temple and waited as an inside agent for the Lantern Festival assault, when he was to set fires and unsettle the defenders. When the army struck, Xue Yong and the other agents lit fires across the city. Amid the confusion, Liangshan broke through and freed the prisoners. His contribution helped take a strong city, showing that the Sickly Tiger could do more than wield weapons: he could disappear among strangers and carry out unusual assignments.

At the ranking of the heroes, Xue Yong corresponded to the Earthly Hidden Star and took the eighty-fourth seat, serving as an infantry officer available for deployment. Skilled with spear and staff, he could fight at the front or remain concealed as required. He was a versatile leader, useful in both direct battle and unconventional work.

After amnesty, he served in the campaigns against Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La. In the bitter southern war, many Liangshan heroes died, and Xue Yong met his own fate. Fighting around Hangzhou, he was killed amid the clash of armies in imperial service. A performer from Luoyang had entered Liangshan's story through a gift of silver at Jieyang, joined the fellowship and helped breach a city, only to leave his blood on the southern battlefield. When Song Jiang returned and the fallen were honored, Xue Yong was included among them.

His life ran from a military family's decline to a wandering performer's trade, combining an unhealthy appearance with unusual ability. His performance in Jieyang drew him into the Jiangzhou affair, and his work inside Daming helped conquer its walls. Though ranked among the Earthly Fiends, he could adapt, fight openly or act unseen, and made himself valuable. The Sickly Tiger died in service with his weapons and loyalty, living up to the strength promised by his name.
薛永者,河南洛阳人氏也。其祖上原是军官出身,后来家道中落,薛永流落江湖,以使枪棒.ja:
薛永は河南洛陽の出身である。祖先は軍官だったが家運が傾き、江湖を流れ、槍棒の演武と膏薬売りで暮らす大道芸人になった。顔は黄ばみ、痩せ衰えて見えたが、槍棒の腕は優れていた。病んだような姿から「病大虫」と呼ばれる。「大虫」は虎の別称であり、見た目は病身でも技は猛々しく、侮れない虎だという意味である。姿だけで判断してはならず、武器を振れば虎のような勢いを見せた。

初登場は掲陽鎮で、「小遮攔」穆春と「及時雨」宋江に関わる一件だった。江州の掲陽鎮を通る宋江は、薛永の演武を見かけた。来たばかりで土地の事情を知らない薛永は見事な槍棒を披露したが、人垣はできても誰も喝采せず、金も出さない。宋江はその冷遇を気の毒に思い、銀五両を与えた。だがこの鎮は穆弘と穆春の兄弟の縄張りで、旅芸人は先に穆家へ挨拶しなければ商売も褒美も許されなかった。薛永も旅人の宋江も知らず、禁を破ったのである。穆春が飛び出して宋江を詰問し、薛永とも口論になった。遺恨から穆兄弟は荘客を率いて宋江を追い、潯陽江まで追い詰めた。宋江は李俊や張横らに救われてようやく助かった。一本の槍棒の演武が、後の江州の大事件へつながった。

その後、宋江は江州で反詩を題し、黄文炳に陥れられ、戴宗とともに処刑場へ送られた。梁山と江州周辺の好漢は江州を騒がせ、刑場を襲って二人を救った。この集いの後、掲陽鎮の穆弘・穆春、潯陽江の李俊・張横・張順・童威・童猛、そして芸人の薛永らは宋江に従って梁山へ上った。薛永は大道芸をやめ、山寨の頭領となった。

入伙後にも功を立てた。盧俊義と石秀を救う大名府攻略では、呉用の命で乞食に変装して城へ入り、荒れ寺に潜んで内応者となった。元宵の攻城時に火を放ち、守軍を混乱させる役である。梁山が実際に攻めると、薛永らは各所で放火し、城内は乱れた。大軍は大名府を破って二人を救出し、薛永の内応も堅城攻略の一助となった。槍棒だけでなく、姿を隠して特別な任務を果たす力も備えていたのである。

席次では地幽星に応じる第八十四位となり、歩軍の将校として命に応じた。槍棒に熟達して前線で戦え、必要なら潜伏もできる。正攻にも奇策にも用いられる、融通の利く頭領だった。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶、方臘の征討に従軍した。江南の激戦では好漢が数多く倒れ、薛永の運命も尽きた。杭州一帯を転戦する中、乱軍の交戦で戦死し、王事に身を捧げた。洛陽の芸人が掲陽鎮の銀の褒美をきっかけに梁山と結ばれ、入伙して内応で城を破る功を立てながら、最後は江南を血で染めた。宋江の凱旋後、戦死した将佐が追贈された際には、薛永もその列に含まれた。

将門に生まれて芸人へ流れ、病んだ姿に優れた腕を隠した一生だった。掲陽鎮の演武は江州の事件につながり、大名府の内応は堅城を破る助けとなった。地煞の一員ながら、屈伸を知り、武にも奇にも応じられる有用な好漢である。痩せた「病大虫」は槍棒と忠義をもって王事に倒れ、虎の名に背かなかった。

燕青，北京大名府人氏，自幼父母双亡，孤苦伶仃，幸得河北玉麒麟卢俊义收养在府中，做.en:
Yan Qing was born in Daming, the Northern Capital. Orphaned young, he was taken into the household of Lu Junyi, Hebei's Jade Qilin, as a personal attendant. Lu recognized his intelligence and competence and deliberately cultivated his talents, keeping him close to handle accounts, carry messages and conduct business. Raised and taught in the Lu household, Yan Qing developed a deep bond with his master and remained unwaveringly loyal to him.

He was handsome, with red lips, white teeth and fine features. Elaborate tattoos covered skin white as silk, giving him a striking appearance unmatched in the city. His abilities were equally remarkable: singing, dancing, wind and string music, and every kind of instrument. He was a superb wrestler, proving himself at the Mount Tai temple in Taian, and an expert with a powerful crossbow whose bolts rarely missed. Elegant in conversation and quick-witted, he spoke regional dialects and understood the slang and ways of every social class. His charm, intelligence and freedom of manner without loss of character earned him the name Wanderer.

He joined Liangshan because of Lu Junyi's downfall. To recruit Lu, Wu Yong posed as a fortune teller, warned of bloody disaster unless Lu traveled southeast, and induced him to write an acrostic rebellious poem on his wall. Lu took the journey and was lured to Liangshan, where he stayed many days before being released. Meanwhile, his steward Li Gu, who was having an affair with Lu's wife Jia, seized the household property and reported the poem as proof that Lu conspired with the outlaws. On his return, Lu was arrested and sent to death row. Everyone in the household feared Li Gu except Yan Qing. Expelled for refusing to betray his master, he begged in the streets but stayed in Daming to seek a chance to save him.

When Lu Junyi was escorted toward Shamen Island, Li Gu bribed the officers Dong Chao and Xue Ba to murder him in a secluded place. Yan Qing followed secretly and hid in the woods. As they prepared to strike, he shot each officer with his crossbow and rescued Lu. Later Lu was captured again and brought back to Daming for execution. Yan Qing went to Liangshan for help, leading to the rescue at the scaffold and the great assault on Daming. Once Lu was freed, master and attendant joined Liangshan together.

At the great assembly, Yan Qing took thirty-sixth place, last among the Heavenly Spirits, corresponding to the Heavenly Skillful Star. He gathered intelligence and campaigned with the army, and his resourcefulness and social gifts made him useful for inquiries, messages and negotiations in both streets and official circles. When Song Jiang sought an imperial amnesty, Yan Qing found a route through Li Shishi, the capital courtesan whom Emperor Huizong visited secretly. His flute playing and tattoos won her favor; he also called her his elder sister. Through her he reached the emperor and helped bring about amnesty. On Lantern Festival night he met Huizong in her house, pleaded Liangshan's case and secured a pardon. The tales of his clever defeat of the Pillar Propping the Sky and his moonlit meeting with the Daoist Emperor display his deftness at its finest.

After amnesty, Yan Qing fought Liao, Tian Hu, Wang Qing and Fang La. His crossbow killed enemy officers, and he repeatedly served as scout and envoy. But he understood that once the birds were gone, the good bow would be put away. When Fang La was defeated, he foresaw that the court would not tolerate these meritorious former outlaws. He urged Lu Junyi to retire with him under hidden names, but Lu refused. One midnight, Yan Qing left a farewell letter, took a carrying load of gold, jewels and valuables, and vanished into the wider world. His final whereabouts were unknown, but he escaped the coming danger. Born among ordinary people and raised in a wealthy house, he combined many talents with loyalty, saved his master and opened the palace's doors. His clear understanding of fortune's rise and fall let him leave freely: one of the rare Liangshan heroes to bring his story to a graceful end.
燕青，北京大名府人氏，自幼父母双亡，孤苦伶仃，幸得河北玉麒麟卢俊义收养在府中，做.ja:
燕青は北京大名府の人で、幼くして両親を失った。孤独な彼を河北の「玉麒麟」盧俊義が屋敷へ引き取り、身近な従者とした。賢く気が利き、仕事のできる少年を見て、盧俊義は心を込めて育て、帳面や資源の管理、伝言や用事を任せた。盧家で養育と教えを受けた燕青と主人の情は深く、生涯その忠義を変えなかった。

燕青は唇が赤く歯が白い端正な顔立ちで、白絹のような肌一面に美しい刺青があった。錦のような姿は城内に並ぶ者がなく、才能も多彩だった。吹奏、弾奏、歌、舞、さまざまな楽器に通じ、相撲も天下に敵なしといえるほどで、泰安州の岳廟でも腕を示した。強い弩を引き、百歩先を射抜く腕もある。話しぶりは風雅で機転に富み、各地の方言や市井の言葉、あらゆる階層の暮らしを知っていた。美しく聡く、江湖を漂っても本性を失わないことから、「浪子」と呼ばれた。

梁山入りは盧俊義の受難に始まる。呉用は盧俊義を誘うため占い師に扮し、流血の災いを避けるには東南へ旅立つべきだと告げ、壁には各句の頭を読むと反逆になる詩を書かせた。盧俊義は策と知らず旅に出て梁山へ誘われ、何日も留められてから帰された。その留守に、妻の賈氏と通じていた家令李固が家財を奪い、反詩を証拠に主人が梁山と謀反を企てたと訴えた。戻った盧俊義は死囚牢へ入れられる。屋敷中が李固を恐れる中、燕青だけは主人を裏切らず、追い出されて乞食となっても、救う機会を待って大名府を離れなかった。

盧俊義が沙門島へ送られる途中、李固は護送役の董超と薛覇を買収し、人目のない場所で殺そうとした。燕青は密かに後を追って林へ隠れ、二人が手を下そうとした瞬間、弩で一人ずつ射倒して主人を救った。だが盧俊義は再び捕らえられ、大名府で処刑されようとした。燕青は梁山へ救援を求め、刑場救出と大名府攻略の大戦につながった。主人が救い出されると、ともに梁山へ上り、燕青も頭領となった。

大聚義では天巧星に応じる第三十六位、天罡の末席に座った。情報収集と従軍を務め、機転と交際の巧みさから、市井や官府での聞き込み、伝言、折衝にも多く用いられた。宋江が招安を求めた時、燕青は東京の名妓李師師に近づいて道を開いた。徽宗が密かに訪れる彼女のもとで、笛と刺青で歓心を得、姉と呼ぶ仲になり、皇帝へ通じたのである。元宵の夜には李師師の屋敷で徽宗に会い、事情を述べて梁山の赦免を願った。「智をもって擎天柱を倒す」話や、月夜に道君皇帝と会う話に、その玲瓏たる手腕がよく表れている。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶、方臘との戦いを転戦し、弩で敵将を射ち、斥候や使者としても功を立てた。だが燕青は「鳥が尽きれば良弓はしまわれる」という理を早くから理解していた。方臘を平らげた後、朝廷がこの草莽の功臣を容れないと読み、盧俊義に功成り身を退いて名を隠そうと勧めたが、主人は聞かなかった。燕青は真夜中に別れの手紙を残し、金珠と貴重品を一担持って静かに去り、行方を知る者はなくなった。市井に生まれ、豪門で育ち、多芸と忠義を備え、危難の主人を救い、宮廷でも事を成した。最後には栄枯を見抜いて遠く離れ、禍を免れた。始めから終わりまで己を保ち、自由な結末を得た数少ない俊傑として語り継がれる。

燕顺，绰号「锦毛虎」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地强星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.en:
Yan Shun, the Brocade Tiger, corresponded to the Earthly Strong Star and ranked fiftieth among Liangshan's one hundred and eight. Born in Laizhou, Shandong, he had traded sheep and horses. When he lost his capital and could no longer support himself, he became an outlaw, gathered men in the hills and ruled a stronghold.

He looked fierce: red hair, yellow beard, a thin yellow face and threatening eyes. Yellow body hair gave his skin a mottled, tiger-like appearance, hence Brocade Tiger. The “brocade” described the variegated color; the “tiger” his ferocity and grim looks. Yet this outlaw was straightforward, recognized worthy men and respected fellowship. He was not merely a heartless robber concerned only with wealth and murder. His base was Qingfeng Mountain in Qingzhou, where steep ground and dense woods suited both a camp and the interception of travelers.

Yan Shun held the mountain's first seat, with Wang Ying, the Short-Legged Tiger, and Zheng Tianshou, the Fair-Faced Gentleman, as deputies. Their band raided households and merchants and became feared locally. One day the men brought a traveler up the mountain, intending to cut out his heart for a hangover soup. As Yan Shun was about to act, the captive lamented that Song Jiang should die there. The name startled him. He halted his men, untied the prisoner and discovered that he was indeed Song Gongming of Yuncheng, the celebrated Timely Rain. Yan Shun bowed, horrified at nearly killing the renowned righteous man, and hurried to receive him as an honored guest. He became Song Jiang's admirer and friend.

Later, the lustful Wang Ying abducted the wife of Liu Gao, administrator of Qingfeng Fort, intending to make her his consort. Song Jiang urged her release, and Yan Shun agreed. But she repaid kindness with hostility and caused Liu Gao to arrest Song Jiang, nearly costing him his life. Hua Rong rescued him, with Yan Shun, Wang Ying and Zheng Tianshou bringing the mountain's forces to help. They then resolved to join Liangshan. On the way through Duiying Mountain, they met Lü Fang and Guo Sheng and gathered Shi Yong, the Stone General, Huang Xin, the Suppressor of Three Mountains, and other heroes. Yan Shun abandoned his own chieftainship and joined the greater fellowship.

At the great ranking he took the fiftieth seat under the Earthly Strong Star. He shared duties in warfare and defense, a seasoned fighter among both infantry and cavalry. His former trade and long outlaw life had made him strong, skilled with weapons and bold in a charge. He often fought in coordination with his old Qingfeng companions Wang Ying and Zheng Tianshou, serving at the front or commanding a sector, and earned considerable merit.

Following amnesty, Yan Shun fought north against Liao, then Tian Hu and Wang Qing, campaigning across the empire. When the court ordered the conquest of Fang La, he crossed the river with Song Jiang and fought deep in the southern lands of Wu and Yue. Harsh terrain and formidable enemy generals cost Liangshan more than half its heroes. Yan Shun too was killed in battle by a Fang La officer and did not return. From Qingfeng outlaw to Song Jiang's ally and finally a soldier fallen in the south, the Brocade Tiger ended wrapped for burial after giving his life in battle, true to his courage and fellowship.

After Song Jiang's return, the court granted posthumous honors and shrines to the fallen, including Yan Shun, to receive later worship. An outlaw in station but capable of recognizing righteousness, he had nearly killed Song Jiang, then become his ally through shared hardship. Though his name belonged to the Earthly Fiends, his conduct showed the fortitude and generosity of a true hero.
燕顺，绰号「锦毛虎」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地强星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.ja:
燕順は「錦毛虎」と呼ばれ、地強星に応じる地煞の一員で、梁山百八人の第五十位に座った。山東莱州の生まれで、もとは羊や馬を売る商人だった。元手を失って暮らせなくなり、山賊となって人を集め、一寨の主になった。

姿は凶悪で、赤い髪と黄色い髭、黄ばんで痩せた顔、鋭い目を持ち、肌には黄色い毛が生えて虎の斑のように見えた。それが「錦毛虎」の由来である。錦毛は髪や肌の入り混じる色を、虎は猛々しい気性と顔を表した。とはいえ性格は率直で、人物の価値を見分け、義気を何より尊んだ。金と殺ししか考えない無情な賊ではなかった。本拠の青州清風山は険しく森も深く、兵を置いて往来を襲うのに適した土地だった。

燕順は第一の座に座り、「矮脚虎」王英と「白面郎君」鄭天寿を副寨主とした。三人は家や商旅を襲い、清風山一帯で勢力を持った。ある日、手下が旅人を捕らえ、腹を裂いて心臓を取り、酔い覚ましの汁にしようとした。手を下す直前、囚人が「宋江がここで死ぬとは惜しい」と嘆いた。名を聞いた燕順は驚いて皆を止め、自ら縄を解いて確かめると、名高い鄆城の「及時雨」宋公明その人だった。天下に知られる義士を殺しかけたと悔やみ、拝礼して酒宴を設け、上客としてもてなした。以後、その人柄に心服して知己となった。

後に好色な王英が清風寨の知寨劉高の妻をさらい、妻にしようとした。宋江が解放を勧め、燕順は従ったが、女は恩を仇で返し、宋江を劉高に捕らえさせて命の危険に陥れた。花栄の救援に加え、燕順、王英、鄭天寿も清風山の軍を率いて下り、宋江を救った。その後、一同は梁山入りを決めた。道中の対影山では呂方と郭盛に会い、「石将軍」石勇や「鎮三山」黄信らも加わり、大勢で水泊へ向かった。燕順は清風山の寨主の座を捨て、大きな義の仲間となった。

大聚義で地強星、第五十位を得た燕順は、他の頭領とともに征戦と防衛を担った。羊馬の商売と長い緑林生活で腕力を鍛え、武器に慣れ、突撃にも勇敢だった。戦では王英や鄭天寿ら清風山の旧友と呼応し、先陣や一方の守りを任され、少なからぬ功を立てた。

招安を受けると、北の遼、続いて田虎、王慶を討ち、南北を転戦した。方臘征討の勅命が出ると宋江と川を渡り、呉越の奥へ進んで激戦を続けた。険しい地形と強い敵将により梁山の好漢は半数以上を失い、燕順も方臘配下の将に陣前で討たれて帰らなかった。清風山の山賊から宋江の盟友となり、南征で命を捧げた錦毛虎の最期は、その半生の勇と義に背くものではなかった。

宋江の凱旋後、朝廷は燕順を含む戦死者に官位を追贈し、廟を立てて後世の祭祀を受けさせた。身は賊でも心は義を知り、一時は宋江を殺しかけながら、患難をともにする盟友となった。地煞の名簿に属していても、その行動は豪侠を示す。水滸の群英に数えられる、貴重な硬骨の男だった。

杨春，绰号「白花蛇」，乃蒲州解良县人氏，应天罡地煞之数，居地隐星，于梁山泊一百单.en:
Yang Chun, nicknamed the White-Spotted Snake, came from Xie County in Puzhou. As the Earthly Hidden Star among the Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Fiends, he ranked seventy-third among Liangshan's 108 heroes and served as an infantry commander. Seven chi tall, with a slightly dark complexion and sharp, vigorous features, he moved like the wind but tempered his rough manner with care. He appeared and vanished in the forests without a trace, wielding a red-tasseled spear that darted like a snake's tongue and recoiled like its sinuous body. His nickname spoke of his elusive movements and ruthless attacks: a patterned snake concealed in the undergrowth, striking too suddenly to guard against.

Born poor, Yang Chun wandered the martial world before becoming an outlaw on Mount Shaohua. There he swore brotherhood with Zhu Wu, the Resourceful Strategist, and Chen Da, the Ravine-Leaping Tiger. The three gathered bandits, raided households, and dominated the surrounding country. Their mountain lay in Huazhou, close to Shi Family Village. Zhu Wu excelled at strategy and formations, Chen Da was fierce and brave, and Yang Chun was adaptable and steady; each contributed his own strengths as one of Shaohua's three chiefs. Short of money and provisions, they planned to take grain from Huayin County, their route passing Shi Family Village. Ignoring Zhu Wu and Yang Chun's advice to take Huayin without provoking Shi Jin, Chen Da insisted on going through the village. There he met Shi Jin, the Nine-Dragoned, whose unpredictable staff work brought him down. Captured alive, Chen Da was tied up at the manor.

Yang Chun and Zhu Wu discussed how to rescue their brother. Zhu Wu proposed appealing through self-sacrifice rather than force. They bound themselves, went straight to Shi Manor, and knelt weeping before Shi Jin, asking to die with Chen Da so that their sworn bond might remain intact. Moved by men who valued brotherhood above life, Shi Jin released Chen Da and entertained all three with food and wine. He thereafter kept close ties with Shaohua, exchanging visits and gifts. When the hunter Li Ji's report exposed Shi Jin's assistance to the outlaws and officials pursued him, he burned his manor and joined Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun on the mountain. These events around Shi Jin's nighttime flight through Huayin and Lu Zhishen's beating of the Bully of the West form Yang Chun's most substantial part in the novel, linking Shaohua to Shi Jin, Weizhou, and Lu Zhishen.

Later, Shi Jin entered Huazhou alone to rescue Yu Jiaozhi and assassinate Prefect He, only to be arrested and imprisoned. Zhu Wu and Yang Chun could find no solution. Lu Zhishen then came to help Shi Jin and was also trapped in Huazhou. Shaohua's small force could not take the city, so Zhu Wu and Yang Chun agreed to send messengers to Liangshan without delay. On hearing their appeal, Song Jiang led a large force to Huazhou, tricked the defenders into opening the gates, killed Prefect He, and rescued Shi Jin and Lu Zhishen. Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and Yang Chun then accompanied Shi Jin to Liangshan, bringing fresh strength to its ranks.

At Liangshan's grand assembly, Yang Chun received the seventy-third seat as the Earthly Hidden Star. He joined Zhu Wu, Chen Da, and others in commanding infantry, regularly advancing with the main force. His practiced spear work and agility made him useful on foot, though he was no warrior capable of facing ten thousand. Among Liangshan's leading fighters, he mostly won credit through cooperation rather than spectacular solo victories or captured standards, as was common among the Earthly Fiends. After the imperial amnesty, he followed Song Jiang north against Liao, then fought Tian Hu in Hebei and Wang Qing in Huaixi by imperial command. Through these campaigns across north and south, he survived repeated battles.

The campaign against Fang La in Jiangnan cost Liangshan dearly, and Yang Chun did not escape. During the assault on Shezhou, a general serving Fang La killed him in battle. He died in imperial service, his blood spilled on the field and his red-tasseled spear forever broken amid Jiangnan's mist and rain. When the court honored those killed in suppressing Fang La, Yang Chun received a posthumous title and a place on the roll of loyal men. The White-Spotted Snake had risen from the wilds and sworn brotherhood on Shaohua, ending his life with courage and loyalty. He never gained great wealth or a prominent court reputation, yet remained true to that brotherhood from beginning to end and upheld the name of a Liangshan hero.
杨春，绰号「白花蛇」，乃蒲州解良县人氏，应天罡地煞之数，居地隐星，于梁山泊一百单.ja:
楊春は蒲州解良県の出身で、渾名は「白花蛇」。天罡地煞のうち地隠星にあたり、梁山泊百八人の第七十三位に列する歩軍頭領である。身の丈七尺、やや浅黒い顔に鋭く精悍な目鼻立ちを備え、風のように素早く歩いた。粗放に見えて細かな気配りもできる男だった。山林に出没して行方をくらまし、得意の朱房の槍は、突けば蛇の舌のように伸び、引けば蛇の体のようにしなった。その神出鬼没な身のこなしと容赦のない一撃が、草むらに潜んで不意に襲う斑蛇を思わせたため、白花蛇と呼ばれたのである。

貧しい家に生まれた楊春は、若いころから江湖を流浪し、やがて少華山で山賊となった。神機軍師の朱武、跳澗虎の陳達と生死を共にする義兄弟となり、三人で手勢を集めて人家を襲い、一帯に勢力を張った。少華山は華州にあり、史家村に近い。朱武は計略と陣法に優れ、陳達は気性が激しく勇敢で、楊春は臨機応変かつ落ち着いていた。それぞれの長所を生かす三人は、少華山の三頭領と呼ばれた。ところが寨の金と食糧が不足し、華陰県へ穀物を取りに行くことになる。その道は史家村を通っていた。朱武と楊春は、史進を刺激せず華陰を先に狙うよう勧めたが、陳達は聞かず、村の通行を強行した。そこで九紋竜の史進と衝突し、変幻自在の棒に敗れて生け捕られ、屋敷に縛り置かれてしまった。

陳達の捕縛を知った楊春は、朱武と救出を相談した。朱武が選んだのは兵を動かすことではなく、自ら苦境に身を置いて情に訴える策だった。二人は自分の身を縛って史家荘へ赴き、史進の前に泣き伏して、義兄弟の誓いを全うするため陳達と一緒に死なせてほしいと願った。義のために命を惜しまぬ二人に心を動かされた史進は、陳達を放し、三人を酒食でもてなした。以来、史進と少華山の間には親交が生まれ、往来や贈り物が続いた。のちに猟師の李吉の密告で山賊への援助が露見すると、史進は追捕を逃れるため屋敷に火を放ち、少華山へ入って朱武、陳達、楊春と寨を守った。史進の華陰県での夜の逃走や、魯智深が鎮関西を殴り殺す挿話の前後にあるこの因縁は、原作で楊春が最も大きな役を担う部分である。少華山はこうして史進を介し、渭州や魯智深とも結ばれた。

その後、史進は玉嬌枝を救い、華州の賀太守を討とうと単身で城へ入ったが、逆に捕らえられて牢へ送られた。朱武と楊春が途方に暮れているところへ、魯智深が義に感じて救出に向かったものの、彼までも華州で囚われる。少華山の兵力では州城を落とせない。朱武と楊春は相談し、使者を昼夜急がせて梁山泊へ救援を求めた。知らせを受けた宋江は大軍を率いて華州へ進み、計略で城門を開かせ、賀太守を殺して史進と魯智深を救い出した。朱武、陳達、楊春の三頭領は史進と共に梁山へ加わり、新たな力となった。

梁山の大集結で席次が定められると、楊春は地隠星として第七十三位に列し、朱武や陳達らと歩軍を率いて各地の戦いに加わった。槍術に熟達し身も軽く、歩戦では頼りになるが、万夫不当の豪傑というほどではない。名将の多い梁山では、単独で敵将を斬ったり旗を奪ったりする華々しい武功より、仲間と協力して功を重ねることが多かった。これも地煞の将にはよく見られる姿である。招安後は宋江に従って遼へ北征し、さらに勅命で河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を討った。南北を転戦して幾度も戦場に立ち、この間は無事に生き抜いた。

しかし江南の方臘討伐では梁山勢の損害が甚だしく、楊春も命を失った。歙州を攻めた際、乱戦の中で方臘配下の大将に討たれ、王事に殉じて戦場に血を流した。朱房の槍は、江南の煙雨の中で永遠に折れたのである。朝廷が方臘討伐の戦死者を追賞すると、楊春にも追封が与えられ、忠義の名簿に記された。草沢に生まれ、少華山で義を結んだ白花蛇は、最後まで忠勇を貫いた。巨万の富や高位を得ることはなかったが、義の一字を初めから終わりまで守り、梁山好漢の名を辱めなかった。

杨林，绰号「锦豹子」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地暗星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.en:
Yang Lin, the Brocade Leopard, was the Earthly Dark Star among Liangshan's 108 heroes, ranking fifty-first overall and belonging to the Earthly Fiends. Originally from Zhangde Prefecture, he came from the outlaw world and roamed far and wide, seeking masters and friends and making the acquaintance of heroes wherever he went.

Yang Lin cut an imposing, handsome figure. He wore a Fanyang felt hat, a parrot-green battle robe, a lion-patterned belt, and black boots that protected his knees. A three-pointed, double-edged blade rose from his back as he traveled with an air of distinction. His bright clothes and armor, agile movements, and brisk, fierce manner suggested the markings and bearing of a leopard, earning him the name Brocade Leopard. Brocade described his colorful dress; leopard conveyed his speed, agility, alertness, and sharp senses. Shrewd and socially adept, he was good at gathering intelligence, guiding travelers, and carrying messages: a particularly capable man among the outlaws.

Yang Lin's arrival at Liangshan owed much to Dai Zong, the Marvelous Traveler. While away on Liangshan business, Dai Zong met him at an inn. Impressed by his appearance, congenial conversation, and established reputation among the outlaws, Dai Zong invited him to join the stronghold. Yang Lin had long heard of Song Jiang's generosity and the heroes gathering at Liangshan and already wished to go there. He gladly accepted. They traveled together toward the marsh, Yang Lin providing directions and relaying messages along the way while both collected news of the martial world. They proved well matched and useful to one another.

Reaching Jizhou, they encountered Yang Xiong, the Sickly Guan Suo, Shi Xiu, the Reckless Third Brother, and other heroes. Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu had killed Pan Qiaoyun and Ying'er and become embroiled in trouble near Zhu Family Manor, and now needed somewhere to settle. Yang Lin already knew Deng Fei, Pei Xuan, and Meng Kang of Yinma River, and helped bring the men together. At the Yinma River stronghold, all were won over by accounts of Liangshan's brotherhood. Yang Lin and Dai Zong then led Deng Fei, Pei Xuan, Meng Kang, Yang Xiong, Shi Xiu, Shi Qian, and their followers, money, and supplies in a great procession to join Liangshan. Delighted by so many new heroes, Song Jiang held a welcoming feast. Yang Lin thereafter took his place among the chiefs in the Hall of Brotherhood.

When the Heavenly Spirits and Earthly Fiends received their seats, Yang Lin became the Earthly Dark Star, ranked fifty-first. The word dark suited his duties: observant and alert, skilled in stealth, reconnaissance, and communication, he often carried confidential reports, guided messengers, and served as Liangshan's eyes, ears, and voice. In battle, he could also charge with his three-pointed, double-edged blade and show considerable strength. During campaigns he often worked closely with Dai Zong, serving as a scout or advance guard and earning credit on many occasions.

After Liangshan accepted the amnesty and entered imperial service, Yang Lin accompanied the army against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, fighting faithfully across north and south. When the court ordered Fang La's suppression, he crossed the Yangtze with Song Jiang into the lands of Wu and Yue and fought bitterly against the rebel forces. Jiangnan's treacherous terrain and formidable enemy commanders inflicted heavy losses on Liangshan. Yang Lin, too, failed to survive the fighting, dying in imperial service before he could return home. The Brocade Leopard's journey led from wandering the martial world to meeting Dai Zong, joining Liangshan, and giving his life in the southern campaign. His death in national service brought an end befitting his years of alertness and chivalry.

When Song Jiang returned, the court honored the fallen. Yang Lin and the other Liangshan brothers killed in battle received posthumous offices and temples where later generations could offer incense. Though his body wandered among the outlaws, his aspirations turned toward loyalty and brotherhood. He brought heroes together to strengthen Liangshan, then fell on a southern battlefield. An Earthly Fiend by rank, he nevertheless added greatly to Liangshan's strength and stands among the novel's alert, courageous, and decisive heroes.
杨林，绰号「锦豹子」，乃梁山泊一百单八将中地暗星，居地煞之列，梁山好汉总座次第五.ja:
楊林は「錦豹子」の渾名を持つ好漢で、梁山泊百八人のうち地暗星にあたり、地煞に属して総席次第五十一位に列する。彰徳府の出身で、緑林に身を置きながら各地を渡り歩き、師や友を訪ねて広く豪傑と交わる流浪の男だった。

堂々たる体つきと立派な顔立ちを備え、頭には范陽のフェルト笠、身には鸚哥色の緑の戦袍、腰には獅子模様の帯、足には膝を守る黒い長靴を着けていた。背には三尖両刃刀を差し、江湖を歩く姿には並々ならぬ気品があった。華やかな衣服と甲冑、しなやかで素早い動き、精悍できびきびした振る舞いが豹を思わせたため、人々は錦豹子と呼んだ。「錦」は鮮やかな装いを、「豹子」は俊敏な身のこなしと鋭い警戒心を表している。機転が利き、世渡りにも長け、人付き合いがうまい。情報集めや道案内、連絡の取り次ぎを得意とする、緑林でも得難い働き手だった。

楊林の梁山入りには、神行太保の戴宗が深く関わっている。梁山の用務で山を下りた戴宗は、旅の途中の宿で楊林と出会った。風采もよく、話も合い、緑林で名の知られた好漢であると知ると、山へ来て仲間になるよう誘った。楊林は、宋公明が義に厚く財を惜しまず、天下の英雄を梁山泊へ集めていると以前から聞き、身を寄せたいと考えていたので、喜んで承諾した。二人は連れ立って梁山へ向かい、楊林は道案内や連絡を担った。道中ではさまざまな江湖の情報も得て、互いの力を生かすよい組み合わせとなった。

薊州に至ると、病関索の楊雄、拚命三郎の石秀らとも出会った。楊雄と石秀は潘巧雲や迎児を殺し、祝家荘付近でも騒動に関わったため、身を落ち着ける場所を求めていた。楊林は飲馬川の鄧飛、裴宣、孟康らと旧知で、その縁を使って一同を結びつけた。飲馬川の山寨に集まった好漢たちは、梁山の大義を聞いてそろって心を動かされた。こうして楊林と戴宗は、鄧飛、裴宣、孟康、楊雄、石秀、時遷らを手勢や金銭、食糧ごと率い、大挙して梁山泊へ向かった。多くの好漢が加わったことを宋江は大いに喜び、酒宴を開いて祝った。楊林も以後、聚義庁に並ぶ頭領の一人となった。

梁山の大集結で天罡地煞の席次が定まると、楊林は地暗星として第五十一位に列した。この「暗」の字は、彼の役目にふさわしい。警戒心と観察力に富み、潜行して敵情を探り、情報を届けることに長けていたため、寨では機密の伝達や道案内を多く担い、梁山の耳目と声の役を果たした。戦場では背の三尖両刃刀を取って突撃する勇力もある。遠征のたびに戴宗らと連携し、斥候や先鋒となって幾度も功を立てた。

招安を受けて梁山が朝廷に従うと、楊林は大軍と共に遼を征し、続いて田虎、王慶を討ち、南北の戦場で力を尽くした。江南の方臘討伐が命じられると、宋江に従って長江を渡り、呉越の奥へ進んで方臘軍と激戦を繰り広げた。江南では地形が険しく敵将も強勇で、梁山の好漢たちは甚大な損害を受けた。楊林もこの戦いを生き残れず、陣前で王事に殉じ、故郷の土を再び踏むことはなかった。江湖をさすらう一頭の錦豹子が、戴宗と知り合い、水泊の仲間となり、ついには南征で命を捧げる。その国事に殉じた結末は、長年の機敏さと侠気に恥じぬものだった。

宋江の凱旋後、朝廷は戦死した諸将を追悼し、楊林と梁山の兄弟たちに官位を追贈し、祠を建てて後世の祭祀を受けさせた。楊林の生涯を見れば、身は緑林を漂いながら、志は忠義へ向かっていた。群雄をつないで水泊を支え、南国へ進んで戦場に命を落としたのである。位は地煞でも、その才は梁山を大いに強めた。『水滸伝』の群像の中でも、機敏さと勇敢な決断力を持つ好漢の一人といえよう。

杨雄，河南府人氏，因随叔伯流落到蓟州，在蓟州两院充当押狱、兼充市曹行刑刽子手，专.en:
Yang Xiong came from Henan Prefecture and drifted to Jizhou with an uncle. He served as a prison officer in the city's two courts and also as the public executioner, overseeing jail matters and beheading condemned prisoners. His somewhat yellow complexion gave him a sickly look, but he had an imposing build, exceptional strength, skill with a long-handled broadsword, and expertise in execution. The people of Jizhou thought his martial prowess and fierce conduct recalled the famed warrior Guan Suo, despite his waxy face. They therefore called him the Sickly Guan Suo, joining Guan Suo's valor to Yang Xiong's unhealthy-looking complexion.

In Jizhou he married Pan Qiaoyun, the daughter of Butcher Pan and widow of Clerk Wang. Honest and loyal, Yang Xiong nevertheless often slept at the prison because of his duties and neglected his household. One day, returning from an execution, he was harassed in the street and rescued by Shi Xiu. The two found themselves kindred spirits and swore brotherhood. Shi Xiu went home with him and helped Butcher Pan reopen his meat shop.

Pan Qiaoyun, however, was secretly having an affair with Pei Ruhai, a monk of Bao'en Temple. Perceptive Shi Xiu noticed the signs, discovered the secret signal given by a wandering monk at dawn, and investigated until he knew the truth. He told Yang Xiong, but Pan Qiaoyun accused Shi Xiu of molesting her. Believing his wife, Yang Xiong grew estranged from his brother, closed the meat shop, and drove him away. Knowing the truth and determined to remove his brother's disgrace, Shi Xiu waited at midnight in the alley the monk used. He first killed Hu Dao, who gave the dawn signal, then the adulterous Pei Ruhai, leaving both bodies and their clothing in the street to expose the affair.

Shi Xiu found Yang Xiong and explained everything in detail. Realizing he had wronged his brother, Yang Xiong was ashamed and furious. They devised a plan, and Yang Xiong lured his wife and her maid Ying'er onto Cuiping Mountain. He first made Ying'er confess the affair from beginning to end. Enraged, he killed her, then tied Pan Qiaoyun to a tree, cut open her belly, and tore out her heart, dismembering his unfaithful wife to avenge his humiliation. The killing on Cuiping Mountain displays Yang Xiong's fierce temperament and absolute love and hatred, and is one of the novel's famously gruesome episodes.

After the murders, Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu had nowhere to hide and discussed joining Liangshan. They met Shi Qian, a chicken thief, and traveled with him. Passing Zhu Family Manor, Shi Qian stole and ate the innkeeper's dawn-crowing rooster, causing a dispute that ended with his capture by the manor. Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu sought help at Liangshan, setting off the three assaults on Zhu Family Manor. They then formally joined the stronghold as chiefs.

At Liangshan's grand assembly, Yang Xiong ranked thirty-second among the Heavenly Spirits as the Heavenly Prison Star. He commanded infantry with Shi Xiu and was often assigned to guard passes, investigate, and make arrests. His background in official service and knowledge of criminal cases and constables' work particularly suited him to such duties. In Liangshan's subsequent campaigns he fought bravely with his long-handled broadsword. Though no great spearhead commander capable of holding an entire front alone, he served diligently and accumulated many modest achievements.

Following the amnesty, Yang Xiong accompanied Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing, fighting tirelessly across north and south. The later bitter campaign against Fang La left Liangshan's men dead and wounded in great numbers. After Fang La's defeat, on the return toward court, Yang Xiong developed a malignant sore on his back. At Hangzhou its poison overwhelmed him, and he died in the army. The Sickly Guan Suo had worn an ailing face all his life, executed countless men, and personally killed his wife on Cuiping Mountain. Fierce to the end, he nevertheless succumbed to a carbuncle on the road before enjoying the honors and prosperity promised after the amnesty. His fate lent the word sickly in his nickname a mournful, prophetic quality. He and Shi Xiu were as close as brothers, sharing adversity in life and dying not far apart. Their bond remains a memorable example of fellowship among the heroes of Water Margin.
杨雄，河南府人氏，因随叔伯流落到蓟州，在蓟州两院充当押狱、兼充市曹行刑刽子手，专.ja:
楊雄は河南府の出身で、叔父に従って薊州へ流れ着き、薊州の両院で牢役人を務めるかたわら、市中の刑場で罪人の首を斬る役も担っていた。顔色はやや黄色く病人めいて見えたが、体格は堂々として腕力に優れ、朴刀をよく使い、処刑の技にも熟達していた。薊州の人々は、蝋のような顔色とは裏腹に武芸が高く勇猛な姿を、百戦の名将関索になぞらえた。そこに病み衰えたような容貌を重ね、「病関索」と呼ぶようになったのである。

薊州で妻に迎えた潘巧雲は、肉屋の潘公の娘で、先夫の王押司を亡くしてから楊雄と再婚した。楊雄は実直な男だったが、公務のため牢で夜を明かすことが多く、家庭を顧みる暇が乏しかった。ある日、処刑を終えて帰る途中に路上で侮辱を受け、一人の好漢に助けられた。それが石秀である。二人は意気投合して義兄弟となり、石秀は楊雄の家に入り、潘公が肉屋を再開するのを手伝った。

ところが潘巧雲は、報恩寺の僧、裴如海と密かに通じていた。細心な石秀は早くから不審を覚え、夜明けを告げる頭陀の合図もつかんで、密通の実情を突き止めた。楊雄に知らせると、潘巧雲は逆に、石秀が自分に言い寄ったと訴えた。妻の言葉を信じた楊雄は石秀を遠ざけ、肉屋を閉じて追い出してしまう。真相を知る石秀は、兄の恥を取り除こうと、真夜中に僧の通る路地で待ち伏せた。まず合図役の頭陀、胡道を殺し、次いで姦僧の裴如海を殺すと、二人の死体と衣服を往来に残し、密通を世間に明らかにした。

石秀から詳しい事情を聞いた楊雄は、弟分を疑った誤りを悟り、恥と怒りに駆られた。二人で策を決め、楊雄は妻と侍女の迎児を翠屏山へ誘い出した。山上でまず迎児に密通の一部始終を白状させると、激怒して彼女を殺し、続いて潘巧雲を木に縛りつけた。そして自ら腹を裂き心臓をえぐり、裏切った妻を切り刻んで屈辱を晴らした。翠屏山の妻殺しは、楊雄の剛烈さと愛憎の激しさを示す場面であり、『水滸伝』でもとりわけ凄惨な挿話として知られる。

殺人の後、楊雄と石秀は身を置く場所を失い、梁山へ行こうと相談した。そこへ鶏泥棒の時遷が現れ、三人は連れ立って旅に出た。祝家荘を通った際、時遷が宿の朝を告げる雄鶏を盗んで食べたことから騒動となり、荘の者に捕らえられてしまう。楊雄と石秀が梁山へ救援を求めたため、祝家荘を三度攻める大戦へと発展した。二人はこれを機に正式に梁山へ入り、頭領となった。

梁山の大集結では、楊雄は天罡の天牢星にあたり、第三十二位に列した。石秀と歩軍を統率するほか、各所の関門の守備や偵察、探索、捕縛を命じられることも多かった。役所勤めの経験があり、刑事や捕り物に通じていたため、うってつけの任務だったのである。その後の梁山の戦いにも従軍し、朴刀を手に勇敢に敵を討った。先陣を切って一方面を単独で支えるほどの猛将ではなかったが、勤勉に働き、大小の功を重ねた。

招安後、楊雄は宋江に従って遼へ北征し、田虎、王慶も討ち、南北の戦場で怠ることなく戦った。方臘討伐では江南の激戦が続き、梁山勢の死傷者はおびただしい数に達した。方臘が平定され、朝廷へ帰る途中、楊雄は背に悪性の腫れ物を生じた。杭州まで来たところで毒が回り、軍中で病死してしまう。生涯、病める顔色をした病関索は、刑場で多くの首を落とし、翠屏山では自ら妻を惨殺した。剛烈に生きた末に背の腫瘍に倒れ、招安後の恩賞や栄華を味わえなかったのである。その結末には、渾名の「病」の字が予言となったような哀しさがある。石秀とは実の兄弟のように苦難を分かち、死の時も遠く離れなかった。二人の義は、水滸の英雄たちの交わりを語る一つの佳話として残っている。

杨志者，自称三代将门之后，五侯杨令公之孙，关西人氏。其人面皮上生有一大块青记，眉.en:
Yang Zhi, a man of Guanxi, claimed descent from three generations of generals and called himself a grandson of Lord Yang of the Five Marquises. A large blue birthmark covered part of his face, and his fierce expression earned him the name Blue-Faced Beast. Highly skilled in martial arts, he passed the military examinations and became an officer of the Palace Command. He hoped to win honors for his wife and descendants, glorify his ancestors, and restore the Yang family's standing through his abilities. Yet repeated misfortunes marked his life and finally drove him to outlawry.

His troubles began when he was ordered to escort a convoy of ornamental rocks and plants. On the Yellow River, rough weather capsized the vessel and sent its cargo into the water. Losing his office and afraid to return to the capital, he fled from place to place. After hearing of an imperial pardon, he gathered a load of valuables and headed for the Privy Council in the Eastern Capital, hoping to purchase influence and regain his post. Near Liangshan Marsh he encountered Wang Lun's band. Lin Chong, sent down to obtain an initiation offering, fought Yang Zhi for dozens of rounds without a victor. Wang Lun wanted to keep Yang Zhi as a counterweight to Lin Chong, but Yang Zhi insisted on seeking office in the capital and departed. There he exhausted his funds, only for Gao Qiu to reject his request outright. Destitute and stranded, he had no choice but to sell his ancestral saber in the marketplace.

While selling it, he met Niu Er, a notorious capital bully known as the Hairless Tiger. Niu Er demanded demonstrations, harassed him, refused to pay, grabbed for the weapon, and struck him. Finally losing patience, Yang Zhi killed him with the saber. The episode of Yang Zhi selling his blade captures a hero's despair when every road is closed. Afterward he surrendered to the authorities and was tattooed and exiled to Daming Prefecture. Fortunately, Governor Liang recognized his talents and retained him for service. He had Yang Zhi compete against Zhou Jin and Suo Chao, the Impatient Vanguard. Yang Zhi's spear and saber skills matched any opponent, so the delighted governor promoted him to military inspector.

At that year's Dragon Boat Festival, Governor Liang prepared gold, jewels, and other treasures worth a hundred thousand strings of cash as a birthday gift for his father-in-law, Grand Tutor Cai, in the Eastern Capital. This was the birthday convoy, and he entrusted it to Yang Zhi. Well aware of the danger, Yang Zhi disguised his men as merchants, chose secluded routes, traveled in the cool of morning and evening, and drove the soldiers forward with constant lashes. Yet Chao Gai, Wu Yong, Gongsun Sheng, Liu Tang, the three Ruan brothers, and Bai Sheng had already laid their trap. On Huangni Ridge they posed as date merchants and a wine seller, putting a sleeping drug in the wine. Despite his precautions, Yang Zhi could only watch the parched, overheated soldiers drink it and collapse one by one. The clever seizure of the birthday convoy became his greatest defeat. All the treasure was taken, and, knowing the punishment awaiting him, he abandoned the escort and fled alone rather than return to Daming.

With nowhere left to turn, Yang Zhi tried to throw himself from a cliff, but someone dissuaded him. He then made for Mount Erlong to become an outlaw. On the way he met Lu Zhishen, the Tattooed Monk. Together they captured Baozhu Monastery on the mountain and became chiefs of its stronghold; Wu Song later joined them. After the three mountain bands attacked Qingzhou, the Erlong men joined Liangshan. At the grand assembly, Yang Zhi ranked seventeenth among the Heavenly Spirits as the Heavenly Dark Star. He commanded cavalry and was a valiant officer below the Five Tiger Generals. An expert with saber and spear, he had held his own against such renowned fighters as Lin Chong and Suo Chao, a worthy son of a military house.

After the amnesty, Yang Zhi earned merit in Song Jiang's northern campaign against Liao. When the army later marched south against Fang La, he suddenly fell ill at Dantu County in Runzhou and had to remain behind. The army moved on, but he never recovered and died there without taking part in Fang La's defeat. Descended from three generations of generals, he had spent his life seeking honors for his family, only to lose first the ornamental convoy and then the birthday gifts, become an outlaw, and die sick beside the army's route. He was denied even a battlefield death and a horsehide shroud. The name Blue-Faced Beast remained, leaving later generations to mourn his great ambitions and long years of failure.
杨志者，自称三代将门之后，五侯杨令公之孙，关西人氏。其人面皮上生有一大块青记，眉.ja:
楊志は関西の出身で、三代続く将門の後裔、五侯楊令公の孫を自称した。顔には大きな青い痣があり、眉間にも凄みが漂っていたため、江湖では「青面獣」と呼ばれた。武芸に熟達し、武挙に応じて殿司の制使官にまでなった男である。自らの腕で妻子に栄誉をもたらし、祖先の名を高め、楊家の家門を再興したいと願っていた。しかし運命は厳しく、生涯にわたって苦境が続き、ついには山賊となった。

初めに命じられたのは、花石綱の護送だった。ところが黄河で風波に遭い、船が覆って献上品を水中に失ってしまう。官職を失った楊志は都へ戻る勇気もなく、各地を逃げ回った。のちに赦免が出たと聞くと、金銀財物を一荷にまとめ、東京の枢密院で復職の手づるを求めようとした。梁山泊のほとりでは王倫の一党と出会い、投名状を求めて山を下りていた林冲と数十合戦ったが、勝負はつかなかった。王倫は林冲を牽制するため楊志を引き留めようとしたものの、楊志は都で官を求める意思を変えずに去った。だが東京に着くと、手持ちの金は尽き、復職の願いも高俅に一蹴された。落ちぶれて旅費すらなくなり、やむなく先祖伝来の宝刀を町で売ることになった。

刀を売っているところへ現れたのが、東京の有名な無頼漢、「没毛大虫」の牛二だった。刀の切れ味を試させたうえで難癖をつけ、金を払わず刀を奪おうとし、さらに楊志に殴りかかった。堪忍袋の緒が切れた楊志は、怒りに任せて牛二を斬り殺してしまう。「楊志売刀」の一段には、行き場を失った英雄の悲哀が描かれている。楊志は自首し、刺青を施されて大名府へ流された。幸いにも留守司の梁中書が才能を認め、配下に置いて周謹や急先鋒の索超と武芸を競わせた。槍でも刀でも引けを取らぬ腕を見た梁中書は大いに喜び、管軍提轄に引き立てた。

その年の端午、梁中書は舅の蔡太師の誕生日を祝うため、十万貫相当の金銀珠玉を東京へ送ろうとした。これが生辰綱であり、護送の大任を楊志に託したのである。危険をよく知る楊志は、商人に変装して人目の少ない道を選び、朝夕の涼しい時刻に進み、兵を休みなく鞭打って急がせた。だが晁蓋、呉用、公孫勝、劉唐、阮氏三兄弟、白勝の八人は、すでに罠を張っていた。黄泥岡で棗売りと酒売りに化け、酒に眠り薬を仕込んだのである。楊志がどれほど警戒しても、暑さと渇きに耐えられない兵たちは薬酒を飲み、次々と倒れた。生辰綱を知略で奪われたこの事件は、楊志の生涯最大の挫折となった。十万貫の財宝をすべて失い、重罪を悟った彼は大名府へ戻れず、一行を捨てて一人で逃げ出した。

追い詰められた楊志は崖から身を投げようとしたが、人に止められ、二竜山へ向かって山賊になる道を選んだ。途中で花和尚の魯智深と出会い、力を合わせて二竜山の宝珠寺を奪い、寨主となった。のちには武松も加わった。三山の勢力が青州を攻めた後、二竜山の一党は梁山へ合流する。大集結の席次では天罡の第十七位、天暗星となり、馬軍を率いて五虎将に次ぐ勇将に数えられた。刀槍を得意とし、林冲や索超と渡り合っても劣らぬ腕は、まさしく将門の子にふさわしかった。

招安後、楊志は宋江に従って遼へ北征し、戦功を挙げた。のちに方臘討伐のため南下した際、潤州丹徒県で急に病に倒れ、軍について進めず、その場で療養することになった。大軍が去っても病は癒えず、ついには丹徒県で没し、方臘平定の戦いに加わることもなかった。三代の将門を継ぐ男は、妻子を栄えさせようと願い続けながら、花石綱と生辰綱を相次いで失い、山賊となり、最後は行軍の途上で病死した。馬革に包まれて戦場に果てる機会さえ与えられなかったのである。残った青面獣の名からは、大きな抱負と半生の不遇がしのばれ、後世の人々の嘆息を誘う。

郁保四者，青州人氏，水浒一百单八将中身材最为高大的一条好汉。其人生得身长一丈，腰.en:
Yu Baosi came from Qingzhou and was the tallest of Water Margin's 108 heroes. A full zhang in height, broad around the waist, handsome and extraordinarily massive, he stood out even among their greatest giants. Seen approaching from afar, he resembled a towering ceremonial deity, and people called him the Guardian of Perilous Roads. This deity was the enormous clay or wooden figure carried at the front of traditional funeral processions to clear the way and drive off evil, often more than a zhang tall. The nickname referred directly to Yu Baosi's exceptional stature and imposing appearance; no other figure of the martial world surpassed his reputation for sheer size.

Yu Baosi did not originally belong to Liangshan's side. Earlier an outlaw near Mount Erlong in Qingzhou, he was employed as an instructor by the Zeng family at Zengtou Market. The settlement had been founded by Elder Zeng, a man from the Jin realm. His five sons, known as the Five Zeng Tigers, and instructors Shi Wengong and Su Ding commanded strong troops and horses, making the place a formidable enemy of Liangshan. Chao Gai had personally attacked it, suffered Shi Wengong's poisoned arrow, and died after returning to the mountain. His last command was that whoever captured his killer should become Liangshan's chief, leaving a bitter feud. While serving Zengtou Market, Yu Baosi stole two fine Liangshan horses, the Snow-Stepping Black Steed and the Night-Shining Jade Lion, helping ignite the conflict. When Song Jiang and Lu Junyi attacked again to avenge Chao Gai, Zengtou Market sent Yu Baosi to negotiate. At Liangshan, its strength, brotherhood, and Song Jiang's courtesy toward capable men made him wish to change sides. Wu Yong privately persuaded him, promised him membership, and arranged for him to act as an inside agent. Yu Baosi turned against his employers, coordinating with Liangshan in battle. With Shi Qian and others he stole Zengtou Market's signal-cannon tokens and secretly reported military intelligence, helping Liangshan destroy the settlement and capture Shi Wengong alive to settle Chao Gai's blood debt. His defection and work within the enemy's ranks were the decisive steps in his joining Liangshan.

With these services to his name, Yu Baosi formally joined the stronghold. At the grand assembly he ranked 105th as the Earthly Stalwart Star. Because of his height and commanding appearance, Song Jiang put him in charge of the central army's command banner. This great flag embodied the army's spirit and carried its orders: when it moved, the troops moved; when it fell, confusion followed. Its bearer needed a mighty frame and a firm stance to display its authority. Towering over a zhang tall, Yu Baosi stood before the central ranks with the huge banner in his hands, an imposing sight and the ideal choice for the duty. Though the novel gives him relatively little attention, whenever the army marched or faced an enemy, his enormous figure could be found beneath the command flag. He was vital to the army's presence and dignity.

After the amnesty, Yu Baosi marched north and south with the army, fighting Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing before the final campaign against Fang La. Jiangnan's dangerous rivers and mountains and Fang La's fierce commanders and seasoned troops inflicted terrible losses on Liangshan, staining the southeast with its heroes' blood. Yu Baosi met his end in that brutal war. As the army attacked Hangzhou, he was conspicuous amid the fighting with the command flag in his hands. An officer of Fang La killed him in the melee, and he fell around the same time as Sun Erniang and other companions. The Guardian of Perilous Roads, tall and majestic as a god, could not protect himself through his great frame. Bearing the flag at the front and standing above the others instead made him a target, and he fell amid Jiangnan's flames of war. The giant who had stolen horses, changed allegiance, helped from within enemy lines, and upheld an army's dignity beneath its central banner ultimately perished among the blades of Fang La's campaign as Liangshan's stars scattered. Only his nickname remained to recall his godlike height and imposing presence.
郁保四者，青州人氏，水浒一百单八将中身材最为高大的一条好汉。其人生得身长一丈，腰.ja:
郁保四は青州の人で、『水滸伝』百八人の中でも最も背の高い好漢である。身の丈一丈、腰回りは幾抱えもあり、顔立ちも堂々として、巨漢ぞろいの仲間の中でひときわ抜きん出ていた。遠くから歩いてくる姿が、廟に据えられた大きな神像を思わせたため、江湖の人々は「険道神」と呼んだ。険道神とは、昔の葬列の先頭で担がれ、道を開き邪を払う役を負った泥塑や木彫りの神像で、一丈を超すほど大きい。この渾名は郁保四の雄大な体と際立つ長身を、そのまま形にたとえたものである。背の高さで名を知られる者の中でも、彼に並ぶ者はいなかった。

郁保四は初めから梁山の側にいたわけではない。以前は青州の二竜山付近で山賊をし、その後、曾頭市の曾家に雇われて武芸師範を務めていた。曾頭市は金国人の曾長者が築いた荘で、五人の息子は曾家の五虎と呼ばれ、史文恭、蘇定という師範も加わって強い兵馬を擁し、梁山泊の有力な敵となっていた。かつて晁蓋が自ら大軍を率いて攻めた際、史文恭の毒矢を受けて帰山後に死に、自分を射た者を捕らえた者を梁山の主にせよと遺言したため、深い怨恨が残っていた。曾頭市に仕えていた郁保四は、梁山の名馬、踢雪烏騅と照夜玉獅子の二頭を盗んだこともあり、それも争いを激化させた原因の一つだった。宋江と盧俊義が晁蓋の仇を討つため再び攻めると、曾頭市は郁保四を講和の使者に立てた。梁山の大勢力と厚い義気、宋江が賢者を礼遇する姿を見た郁保四には、すでに帰順の心が芽生えていた。呉用はその機を捉えて密かに説き、入山を認める代わりに内応を頼んだ。郁保四は戦場で寝返り、内外から梁山に協力した。時遷らと曾頭市の合図用の砲と信物を盗み、軍情を密告して、曾頭市の攻略と史文恭の生け捕りを助け、晁蓋の仇討ちに貢献した。曾頭市を離れて内応者となったこの一件が、梁山入りの転機である。

功を立てた郁保四は正式に梁山へ加わり、大集結で席次が決まると、地健星として第百五位に列した。長身で見栄えもよいため、宋江は中軍の帥字旗を専門に持つ役を任せた。大将旗は一軍の魂であり、命令の拠り所でもある。旗が動けば軍が動き、倒れれば軍は乱れる。その威儀を示すには、堂々たる体格と揺るがぬ足取りを持つ好漢が必要だった。一丈余りの郁保四が大旗を手に中軍の前へ立つ姿は実に威風堂々として、この役にこれ以上ふさわしい者はいなかった。原作での記述は多くないが、大軍が出陣し、敵と対峙するたび、帥旗の下には彼の大きな姿があった。軍の体面と威厳を支える、欠かせぬ一人だったのである。

招安後は軍と共に南征北討し、遼を征し、田虎、王慶を平らげ、最後に方臘討伐へ南下した。江南の険しい山河に、方臘配下の猛将と精兵が加わり、梁山の好漢たちは甚大な死傷者を出して東南の地を血で染めた。郁保四もこの苛烈な戦いで最期を迎えた。杭州攻めの乱戦で、帥旗を持つひときわ目立つ姿が敵の目を引き、方臘の部将に討たれたのである。孫二娘らも相次いで倒れ、彼も遠征の途上に命を落とした。神像のようにそびえる険道神も、雄大な体で身を守ることはできなかった。むしろ旗を掲げて前に立つ長身が標的となり、江南の戦火に倒れたのである。馬を盗み、敵方に通じ、戦場で帰順し、やがて中軍の旗の下で一軍の威厳を担った巨漢は、梁山の星々が散る中、方臘討伐の刃に消えた。「険道神」の三文字だけが、道を開く神に似たその並外れた背丈と威風を後世に伝えている。

乐和，绰号「铁叫子」，茅州人氏，应地乐星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十七把交椅。.en:
Yue He, the Iron Whistle, came from Maozhou. He was the Earthly Music Star, ranked seventy-seventh among Liangshan's 108 heroes. Originally a junior jail officer under Sun Li, Dengzhou's military inspector, he was handsome, bright, and quick-witted. He could play every kind of instrument and was especially gifted at singing. His powerful, ringing voice seemed able to pierce clouds and split stone. Hearing a tune once was enough for him to reproduce it, whether a northern or southern song or a simple street melody, all rendered with graceful phrasing. His golden voice earned the name Iron Whistle, suggesting the clear, stirring, enduring tones of an iron flute or bronze gong. Everyone who heard him listened attentively.

Yue He combined his singing with practiced martial skills and considerable ingenuity. His sister had married Sun Li, the Sickly Yuchi, making the two brothers-in-law; this family tie helped bring him to Liangshan. At the time Liangshan was attacking Zhu Family Manor but could not break it through repeated assaults. The manor had hired Luan Tingyu, the Iron Staff, as instructor and formed a mutually supporting alliance with Hu and Li Family Manors, making it easy to defend. Wu Yong proposed bringing Sun Li's Dengzhou group inside to coordinate an attack. Sun Li's younger brother Sun Xin, the Little Yuchi, and his wife Gu Dasao, the Tigress, had already become enemies of the authorities by breaking Xie Zhen and Xie Bao out of prison. They had gathered with Zou Yuan, the Forest-Emerging Dragon, Zou Run, the One-Horned Dragon, Yue He, and their companions, intending to join Liangshan.

Yue He accompanied Sun Li, Sun Xin, Gu Dasao, Xie Zhen, Xie Bao, Zou Yuan, and Zou Run, the group called the Seven Heroes of Dengzhou, eight with Yue He included. Pretending to be Dengzhou troops sent to help, they gained entry to Zhu Family Manor. Sun Li and Luan Tingyu had studied under the same master, and this connection allowed the newcomers to settle openly inside and win the Zhus' trust. When Liangshan attacked, Yue He and the others suddenly rose within, striking in coordination with the army outside and catching the manor unprepared. Yue He's alert responses and skill in dealing with the household without revealing the plot contributed greatly to the plan, helping Liangshan overrun the three allied manors. The three assaults marked a major stage in Liangshan's growth, and the Dengzhou group's deception was crucial to victory. Yue He's part in it is his most conspicuous achievement in the novel.

After the victory, Yue He went to Liangshan with Sun Li's group. His musical knowledge, fine voice, intelligence, and resourcefulness soon proved useful. At feasts, celebrations, welcomes, and farewells, he sang to enliven the drinking and please the company, taking part in much of the stronghold's music and ceremony. At the grand assembly he received the seventy-seventh seat as the Earthly Music Star, a title perfectly suited to his exceptional singing. Though no fierce general famed for charging and killing enemy commanders, he possessed rare musical understanding and quick wits. His ability to respond to changing circumstances also made him particularly useful in intelligence work, deception, and operations requiring inside help.

Following the imperial amnesty, Yue He joined Song Jiang against Liao, Tian Hu in Hebei, Wang Qing in Huaixi, and finally Fang La in Jiangnan. Fighting across north and south, his quick thinking helped him survive repeated battles, making him one of the heroes whose story ended well. After Fang La's defeat and the army's return, the court distributed rewards. His rare singing voice and pleasing, clever manner led to his being retained in the capital and assigned to the household of Imperial Son-in-Law Wang. There he supplied music, taught songs, and entertained his patrons, living peacefully into old age. Yue He won his place through a golden voice and adaptable wit rather than fame in bloody combat. From Dengzhou through Liangshan's rise and decline, his singing ultimately allowed him to withdraw unharmed and remain in the capital. Among 108 heroes so many of whom died on campaign, the Iron Whistle's clear, lingering note provides an unusually fortunate and distinctive ending.
乐和，绰号「铁叫子」，茅州人氏，应地乐星，于梁山泊一百单八将中坐第七十七把交椅。.ja:
楽和は茅州の出身で、渾名は「鉄叫子」。地楽星にあたり、梁山泊百八人の第七十七位に列する。もとは登州の兵馬提轄、孫立のもとで小さな牢役人を務めていた。眉目秀麗で利発、あらゆる楽器を扱い、とりわけ歌に優れていた。高く澄んだ声は雲を貫き石を裂くように響き、どのような曲でも一度聞けば節を覚えて歌えた。南北の歌から巷の小唄まで、自在に情感を込めて歌いこなしたのである。その美声を、鉄笛や銅鑼のように清らかで力強く長く響く音になぞらえ、人々は鉄叫子と呼んだ。歌声を耳にした者は、誰もが聞き入った。

楽和は歌だけでなく武芸にも熟達し、機転と知恵を備えた文武両道の才人だった。姉が病尉遅の孫立に嫁いでいたため、二人は義理の兄弟でもある。この縁が梁山入りの鍵となった。当時、梁山勢は祝家荘を攻めていたが、度重なる攻撃でも落とせずにいた。鉄棒の欒廷玉が師範を務め、扈家荘、李家荘とも連携して互いに支え合うため、守りやすく攻めにくかったのである。呉用は登州の孫立一党を引き入れ、内外から協力して荘を破る策を考えた。孫立の弟、小尉遅の孫新と、その妻、母大虫の顧大嫂は、解珍と解宝を救う牢破りによってすでに官府と敵対していた。出林竜の鄒淵、独角竜の鄒潤、鉄叫子の楽和らも集まり、梁山へ向かおうとしていた。

楽和は孫立、孫新、顧大嫂、解珍、解宝、鄒淵、鄒潤と共に、いわゆる「登州七雄」、楽和を数えれば八人の一行として、援軍に来た登州の兵だと偽り、祝家荘へ入った。孫立と欒廷玉は同門の兄弟弟子だったため、一党は堂々と荘内に滞在し、祝家の信用を得ることができた。梁山軍が攻め寄せると、楽和らは荘内で突然蜂起し、外の軍と呼応して不意を突いた。楽和は機敏に立ち回り、荘の人々と接しても綻びを見せず、この潜入作戦に大いに力を貸した。こうして梁山は祝家を中心とする三荘を一挙に制した。祝家荘への三度の攻撃は梁山拡大の大きな節目であり、登州一党の偽装潜入は勝利の要となった。その一翼を担ったこの働きが、原作で楽和の才が最もよく現れる場面である。

祝家荘が落ちると、楽和も孫立の一党と共に梁山へ入った。歌と音楽の知識、聡明さと臨機応変の才は、山でもさまざまに役立った。宴会や祝い、客の歓迎や送別のたびに声を張って歌い、酒席を盛り上げ、人々を楽しませた。寨の歌舞音曲や儀礼にも広く関わった。大集結で席次が定められると第七十七位、地楽星となる。この星名は、優れた歌声を持つ彼の本領にぴったりだった。敵将を斬って突進する猛将ではないが、軍中では得難い音楽の才と利発さを備え、状況に応じて動けたため、諜報や敵を欺く仕事、内応を伴う作戦にもよく役立った。

招安後、楽和は宋江に従って遼を征し、河北の田虎、淮西の王慶を討ち、さらに江南の方臘討伐へ南下した。南北を転戦する中でも機敏さを生かして幾度もの戦場を生き抜き、梁山の中ではよい結末を得た一人となった。方臘平定後、軍が帰還して恩賞が与えられると、世にまれな美声と利発で愛嬌のある人柄を買われ、都に留められた。そして駙馬都尉の王都尉の屋敷に配され、音楽を供し、歌を教え、人々を楽しませる楽人となって、平穏な老後を送ったのである。鉄叫子の楽和は血戦の名声ではなく、美声と機転で身を立てた。登州から梁山の盛衰に付き従い、最後は歌の才によって無事に退き、都で仕えた。百八人の多くが戦場に果てる中、その清く長く響く歌声のような穏やかな結末は、ひときわ趣の異なる好漢の幕引きであった。

张横，绰号「船火儿」，应天平星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十八位，乃水军头领之一。其人本.en:
Zhang Heng, the Boatman, was the Heavenly Balance Star, ranked twenty-eighth among Liangshan's heroes and serving as a naval commander. His birthplace is not clearly recorded in the common edition, but he lived around the Xunyang River, earning a living in the riverside underworld alongside his younger brother Zhang Shun. He ferried passengers on the Yangtze and Xunyang rivers, working as a boat hand, the occupation behind his nickname. Yet his business concealed murderous intentions. Outwardly he carried merchants across the water; in darkness, midstream, he offered them a choice of broad-blade noodles or wontons. The first meant a single fatal slash; the second meant being thrown into the river with their luggage. Fierce, ruthless, and dominant on the water, the Boatman was widely feared. Tall, powerfully built, rough-featured, and immensely strong, he favored a pointed knife. Though his swimming could not match Zhang Shun's extraordinary skill, he was an accomplished river man.

He first met Song Jiang on the Xunyang River. While exiled to Jiangzhou, Song Jiang boarded his ferry with two companions. Midstream, Zhang Heng threatened them with his choice of noodles or wontons, terrifying all three. At the critical moment, Li Jun, the River-Churning Dragon, arrived by boat with Tong Wei and Tong Meng. Recognizing Song Jiang, they shouted Zhang Heng down and saved the passengers. Song Jiang thus came to know Zhang Heng and, through him, the even more accomplished swimmer Zhang Shun. Later, after Song Jiang's rebellious poem at Xunyang Tower led to imprisonment and a death sentence, Liangshan's heroes rescued him from the execution ground. Zhang Heng joined Li Jun, Zhang Shun, the three Ruan brothers, Tong Wei, Tong Meng, and the other river fighters in supporting the rescue and gathering at White Dragon Temple. He also helped in the subsequent attack on Wuwei and capture of Huang Wenbing. After the upheaval in Jiangzhou, he followed the others to Liangshan and became a naval chief.

At Liangshan, Zhang Heng commanded the fleet and guarded the water strongholds with Li Jun, Zhang Shun, the Ruan brothers, Tong Wei, and Tong Meng. Water surrounded the mountain on three sides, making the navy fundamental to its defense. Whenever imperial troops attacked by river, he fought desperately from his boat, scuttling and overturning enemy vessels and capturing their commanders alive. He earned merit in the two victories over Tong Guan and three defeats of Gao Qiu. At the grand assembly he became the Heavenly Balance Star among the Heavenly Spirits. He and Zhang Shun stood together as leading naval commanders, a celebrated pair of brothers in Liangshan's fleet.

After the amnesty, Zhang Heng served at the front in naval fighting against Liao, Tian Hu, and Wang Qing. The later campaign against Fang La brought the fleet into Jiangnan's waterways, ideal ground for earning distinction, but his end was tragic. During the fighting around Hangzhou, his desire for military glory and anxiety over Zhang Shun led him to reckless action. Zhang Shun had already died beneath Yongjin Gate, struck by a storm of arrows and sinking into West Lake. Grief-stricken and furious, Zhang Heng sought revenge. Without waiting for orders, he led a naval detachment deep into enemy territory to raid Fang La's inner-city waterways. Ambushed, the entire force was surrounded and captured. The Boatman, long master of the rivers, was taken in this rash advance and soon killed. Another account says that he contracted an epidemic disease and died during the Fang La campaign; the common edition lists him among the many Liangshan men who died sick around Hangzhou. Whether killed in battle or by illness, he never returned home. After the army's return, Song Jiang recounted the navy's achievements, and Zhang Heng received posthumous honors among Liangshan's fallen. Zhang Shun perished in West Lake and Zhang Heng elsewhere in Jiangnan. The brothers who once sailed together and ruled the waves became loyal spirits beneath the water, leaving readers of Water Margin to mourn them.
张横，绰号「船火儿」，应天平星，梁山泊英雄座次第二十八位，乃水军头领之一。其人本.ja:
張横は「船火児」の渾名を持ち、天平星にあたる梁山泊第二十八位の好漢で、水軍頭領の一人である。通行本では本籍がはっきりせず、普段は潯陽江の一帯に暮らし、弟の張順と共に江湖の稼業で生計を立てていた。揚子江や潯陽江で船を操り、人を渡す船頭をしていたのである。船火児とは本来、船の働き手や船頭を指すが、張横の渡し船には殺意が潜んでいた。表向きは旅の商人を対岸へ運びながら、夜の川中では「板刀麺か、饂飩か」と脅して金と命を奪った。板刀麺は一刀で殺すこと、饂飩は荷物ごと水へ投げ込むことを意味した。凶暴で容赦がなく、水上を我が物とする船火児の恐ろしさは広く知られていた。大柄で粗野な顔つき、驚くほどの腕力を持ち、尖った刀をよく使った。泳ぎは弟の神業には及ばないものの、波の上で生きる熟練の男だった。

宋江との出会いも潯陽江で起きた。江州へ流された宋江が、二人の連れと張横の渡し船に乗ると、川の真ん中で張横が悪心を起こし、板刀麺と饂飩のどちらを選ぶかと迫った。三人が恐怖に震える危機に、混江竜の李俊が童威、童猛と船で駆けつけた。宋江を見知っていた彼らが張横を叱りつけ、ようやく命が救われたのである。これを機に宋江は張横と知り合い、その縁で泳ぎにいっそう優れた弟の張順とも結ばれた。のちに宋江が潯陽楼の反詩で投獄され刑場へ引かれると、梁山の好漢たちが救出に動いた。張横も李俊、張順、阮氏三兄弟、童威、童猛ら水上の仲間と援護し、白竜廟に集まった。続く無為軍への攻撃と黄文炳の捕縛にも力を尽くす。江州の大騒動の後は一同と梁山へ入り、水軍頭領となった。

梁山では李俊、張順、阮氏三兄弟、童威、童猛らと水寨を守り、水軍を率いた。三方を水に囲まれた梁山にとって、水軍は守りの根幹である。官軍が水路から攻めるたび、張横は船を駆って死闘を繰り広げ、敵船に穴を開け、転覆させ、敵将を生け捕った。童貫を二度退け、高俅を三度破った戦いにも功績がある。大集結の席次では天罡の天平星に列し、弟の張順と共に水軍の主将となった。兄弟がそろって梁山の水師を支える姿は、佳話として語られた。

招安後は遼、田虎、王慶との戦いに従軍し、水戦では常に先頭を担った。方臘討伐で江南へ進むと、水郷は水軍が功を立てる絶好の場所だったが、張横の結末は悲惨だった。杭州周辺の戦いで、武功への思いと弟の安否への不安が重なり、功を焦って無謀に進もうとしたのである。そのころ張順はすでに湧金門の下で乱矢を受け、西湖の底に沈んでいた。悲憤に駆られた張横は仇を討とうと、命令を待たず水軍の一隊を率いて敵地の奥へ入り、方臘の内城の水路を奇襲しようとした。ところが伏兵に遭い、部隊ごと包囲されて全員が捕らえられた。水上に威を振るった船火児は、この無謀な前進の果てに囚われ、ほどなく殺されたのである。一方、方臘遠征中に疫病を得て死んだという説もある。通行本には杭州一帯で病死した梁山の好漢が多く記され、張横もその一人に数えられる。戦死であれ病死であれ、彼が故郷へ帰れなかったことに変わりはない。宋江の帰還後、水軍の戦功が追叙され、張横にも追封が与えられ、梁山の英霊と共に祀られた。張順は西湖に、張横は江南に果て、かつて並んで船を操り風波を駆けた兄弟は、共に水底の忠魂となった。その最期は『水滸伝』を読む者の胸に哀しみを残す。

张清者，彰德府人氏，原是东昌府的守将。其人善能飞石打人，百发百中，于马上取出石子.en:
Zhang Qing came from Zhangde Prefecture and originally commanded the defense of Dongchang. He was a master at striking opponents with thrown stones, never missing his mark. From horseback he would produce a pebble and flick it into an enemy commander's face, knocking the man from his saddle. Because his stones were sharper and more accurate than feathered arrows, he was called the Featherless Arrow. He had two deputies: Gong Wang, the Flowery-Necked Tiger, whose body bore tiger-pattern tattoos and who threw spears; and Ding Desun, the Arrow-Struck Tiger, scarred across cheek and neck and skilled at throwing forks. All three excelled at projectile weapons, complementing one another.

Zhang Qing's entry into Liangshan, like Dong Ping's, arose from the attacks on Dongping and Dongchang. Song Jiang attacked Dongping while Lu Junyi advanced on Dongchang, agreeing that the first to capture his city should become Liangshan's chief. At Dongchang, Lu Junyi met Zhang Qing. Rather than engage Liangshan's generals in ordinary close combat, Zhang Qing unleashed his stones. One hero after another rode out to challenge him, and he struck each in turn: fifteen Liangshan chiefs were wounded and driven back. Renowned fighters including Xu Ning, the Golden Spear, Zhu Tong, the Beautiful Beard, Shi Jin, the Nine-Dragoned, Mu Hong, the Unrestrained, and Yang Zhi, the Blue-Faced Beast, all suffered blows to the face. Even Huyan Zhuo and Guan Sheng could do nothing. His flying stones shook Liangshan's confidence, halting both armies beneath the walls and leaving Song Jiang and Lu Junyi at a loss. Defeating fifteen Liangshan generals with stones was Zhang Qing's dazzling introduction.

After these heavy setbacks, Liangshan turned to strategy. Song Jiang and Wu Yong used grain carts as bait to lure Zhang Qing outside, preparing an ambush by the water. Unaware of the trap, he led his men to seize the supplies, was surrounded, and was drawn toward the shore. Zhang Shun, the White Streak in the Waves, lay hidden underwater. He toppled Zhang Qing into the river, captured him alive, and brought him to Song Jiang's tent. Song Jiang valued talent. Impressed by Zhang Qing's skill, he sent the attendants back, untied him personally, bowed low, and treated him with every courtesy. Grateful for his life and moved by Liangshan's brotherhood, Zhang Qing surrendered with Gong Wang and Ding Desun. After Dongchang fell, all three formally joined the stronghold.

Zhang Qing arrived just as Liangshan held its grand assembly. His unmatched stone throwing and outstanding achievements won him a place among the Heavenly Spirits, ranked sixteenth as the Heavenly Swift Star. A cavalry commander, he was one of Liangshan's most unusual generals. He relied on projectiles rather than saber and spear, often deciding a confrontation with a single unexpected stone that dropped the opposing commander. He was a master of surprise. Song Jiang later helped arrange his marriage to Qiongying, and husband and wife earned distinction together during the Tian Hu campaign, another celebrated story in the common edition's account of that war.

After the amnesty, Zhang Qing served against Liao and Fang La, repeatedly winning unusual victories. His end, however, was brutal. During the attack on Dusong Pass, Dong Ping insisted on fighting with an injured arm. Close as brothers, Zhang Qing accompanied him to challenge the defenders. In the fighting he pursued an enemy general on horseback and, amid the confusion, entered dangerous ground. Fang La's general Li Tianrun wheeled and thrust his spear into Zhang Qing's throat, and Zhang Qing was killed in the melee. The unfailing Featherless Arrow never found the chance to use his stones, dying by an enemy spear on the same day as his friend Dong Ping at Dusong Pass. His stone throwing had no equal among the 108, yet his life ended in a horsehide shroud. His nickname leaves later generations to recall the tremendous spectacle of the man who once felled fifteen famous commanders.
张清者，彰德府人氏，原是东昌府的守将。其人善能飞石打人，百发百中，于马上取出石子.ja:
張清は彰徳府の出身で、もとは東昌府の守将だった。飛石で人を打つ技に長け、馬上で石を取り出して投げれば百発百中、敵将の顔を狙ってたちまち落馬させた。その鋭さと正確さが羽のある矢にも勝るため、江湖では「没羽箭」と呼ばれた。副将は二人いる。一人は全身に虎の斑紋を彫り、投げ槍を使う「花項虎」の龔旺。もう一人は頬から首にかけて傷痕があり、投げ叉を使う「中箭虎」の丁得孫である。三人はいずれも飛び道具を得意とし、互いの長所をよく補っていた。

張清が梁山へ入る経緯は、董平と同じく、宋江たちによる東平府と東昌府の攻略に始まる。宋江が東平、盧俊義が東昌を攻め、先に城を落とした者を梁山の主にすると約束した。東昌へ進んだ盧俊義を待っていたのが張清である。張清は梁山の諸将と正面から斬り結ぼうとせず、飛石の技を繰り出した。好漢が一人ずつ挑み出るたび石で打ち、十五人の頭領を次々と負傷させて退かせたのである。金鎗手の徐寧、美髯公の朱仝、九紋竜の史進、没遮攔の穆弘、青面獣の楊志ら名将がそろって顔を打たれ、呼延灼や関勝ほどの人物にも打つ手がなかった。一時はその名が梁山を震え上がらせ、宋江と盧俊義の両軍が城下に阻まれて途方に暮れた。飛石で梁山の十五将を打つこの一段は、張清の登場を飾る最も鮮やかな場面である。

大きな損害を受けた梁山勢は、計略で捕らえることにした。宋江と呉用は糧車を餌に城外へ誘い、水辺にあらかじめ伏兵を置いた。罠と知らぬ張清は兵を率いて糧食を奪いに来たが、途中で包囲され、水際へ追い込まれた。水中に潜んでいた浪裏白条の張順が張清を水へ落とし、生け捕りにして宋江の陣へ連れてきた。人材を惜しむ宋江は、張清の腕前に感心し、左右の者を下がらせて自ら縄を解き、身を低くして礼を尽くした。命を助けられた恩と梁山の厚い義気に感じた張清は、龔旺、丁得孫と共に降った。東昌府の陥落後、三人は正式に梁山の仲間となった。

入山はちょうど大集結の時期にあたり、張清は天下に並ぶ者のない飛石の技と際立つ戦功によって天罡に列し、第十六位の天捷星となった。馬軍を率いる、梁山でも異色の将である。刀槍よりも飛び道具を頼みとし、両軍が対峙する一瞬に石一つで勝負を決めた。不意を突かれた敵将はたちまち倒れ、奇策で勝ちを取る名手だった。のちに宋江が瓊英との縁を結び、田虎討伐では夫婦で戦功を立てた。通行本の田虎征伐の諸回に見える、これも梁山の佳話の一つである。

招安後、張清は遼や方臘との戦いに従い、各地でたびたび奇功を挙げた。しかし最期は凄惨だった。独松関を攻めた際、董平が腕の傷を押して戦おうとすると、兄弟同然の張清も付き添い、関の下で敵を挑発した。交戦中、馬を駆って敵将を追った張清は、混乱の中で危険な場所へ踏み込んでしまう。方臘配下の厲天閏が馬を返して放った槍が喉を貫き、張清は乱戦の中で命を落とした。百発百中の没羽箭が石を使う間もなく敵槍に倒れ、親友の董平と同じ日に独松関で死んだのである。飛石の技は百八人の中で随一だったが、天は長い命を許さず、馬革に包まれる結末となった。没羽箭の名は、かつて十五人の名将を打ち倒した威風を後世にしのばせている。

菜园子张青，孟州人氏，乃梁山泊一百单八将中应地刑星的好汉，坐第一百零二把交椅。这.en:
Zhang Qing, the Gardener, came from Mengzhou. He was the Earthly Punishment Star, ranked 102nd among Liangshan's 108 heroes. His early occupation was ordinary enough: he tended vegetables at Guangming Monastery on the Mengzhou road, working the garden and carrying buckets of manure. This earned him his nickname. But he was a rough-tempered man unwilling to remain beneath others. A trivial dispute with the monks provoked him into killing every monk in the monastery and burning it down. He fled into outlawry and began robbing travelers below Big Tree Slope in Mengzhou. His wife was the notorious Sun Erniang, the Female Yaksha. They later opened an inn at Crossroads Slope, specializing in attacks on lone merchants. Drugging the food and wine, they stripped unconscious guests and stole their possessions. Those with good flesh were chopped into filling for human-meat buns; the thin and small were dumped into ditches. This infamous criminal inn spread the couple's fearful reputation throughout the Mengzhou roads.

Yet even the owner of such an establishment kept a code. Ordinary lone merchants were fair prey, but he forbade harm to three sorts of travelers: wandering Buddhist and Taoist clerics, entertainers and prostitutes, and condemned prisoners being escorted into exile. Through these three prohibitions he met two men who later became famous at Liangshan. The first was Lu Zhishen, the Tattooed Monk. After the trouble at Peach Blossom Village and the burning of Waguan Monastery, Lu passed Crossroads Slope and was nearly drugged by Sun Erniang. Zhang Qing returned in time to recognize him and bring him round, and they became friends. The second was Wu Song, the Pilgrim. Exiled to Mengzhou after killing Ximen Qing, he passed the inn. Despite seeing an exile, Sun Erniang tried to drug him, but he discovered the scheme and pinned her to the ground. Zhang Qing returned, called a halt, apologized, and swore brotherhood with Wu Song. Later, when Wu Song had spilled blood at Mandarin Duck Tower and had nowhere to go, the couple disguised him as a wandering Buddhist ascetic and gave him two monk's sabers and a full outfit. His lifelong pilgrim's appearance and name thus came from Crossroads Slope. This shelter and assistance was the clearest expression of Zhang Qing's brotherly loyalty.
